title.zh: 卷十四 志第四 地理上
title.raw: 卷十四 志第四 地理上 Volume 14 Treatises 4: Geography Part One

sentences.zh: 昔者元胎無象，太素流形，對越在天，以爲元首，則記所謂冬居營窟，夏居橧巢，飲血茹毛，未有麻絲者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the primordial embryo had no image, the Grand Simplicity flowed into forms, and humankind faced and served Heaven as the supreme head; thus the records speak of dwelling in earthen pits in winter and nest-like shelters in summer, drinking blood and eating flesh with the hair on, before there was hemp or silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest age, before form took shape from undifferentiated simplicity, people looked to Heaven as their sovereign. The old texts describe them wintering in sunken huts, summering in treetop nests, consuming raw flesh and blood, long before cloth ever existed.

sentences.zh: 及燧人鑽火，庖犧出震，風宗下武，炎胤昌基，畫野無聞，其歸一揆。

translations.literal: When Suiren drilled fire, when Paoxi (Fuxi) issued from the Zhen trigram, when the wind lineage honored the martial below, and the fiery heir established a flourishing foundation, of marking the wilds into fields nothing is heard; they all come to one standard.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Suiren’s discovery of fire, Fuxi’s rise from the east, the succession of wind and flame that laid a prosperous foundation, and though we hear nothing yet of surveying the wilderness into domains, all these ages still point to a single underlying pattern.

sentences.zh: 黃帝則東海南江，登空躡岱，至於崑峰振轡，崆山訪道，[1]存諸汗竹，不可厚誣。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor reached the eastern sea and the southern Yangtze, ascended Kongsang and trod Mount Tai, came to Kunlun’s peaks to rein his horses, and on Mount Kongtong sought the Way; these are preserved on bamboo slips and must not be lightly gainsaid.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor is said to have traveled from the eastern sea to the southern rivers, climbed Kongsang and Mount Tai, climbed the Kunlun heights to pause his chariot, and sought the Dao on Kongtong; the tradition is written on ancient slips and should not be dismissed out of hand.

sentences.zh: 高陽任地依神，帝嚳順天行義。

translations.literal: Gaoyang (Zhuanxu) relied on the earth and trusted the spirits; Emperor Ku followed Heaven and practiced righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu grounded his rule in the land and in communion with the spirits; Emperor Ku aligned his government with Heaven and with moral duty.

sentences.zh: 東踰蟠木，西濟流沙，北至幽陵，南撫交阯，日月所經，舟車所至，莫匪王臣，不踰茲域。

translations.literal: East of Panmu, west crossing the flowing sands, north to Youling, south pacifying Jiaozhi—wherever sun and moon passed, wherever boat and cart could reach, none were not the king’s subjects, and none exceeded this domain.
translations.idiomatic: Their sway ran east beyond the eastern frontier tree, west across the desert sands, north to the dark wastes, and south to Jiaozhi; under sun and moon, wherever chariot or ship could go, every people owed allegiance to the throne, and none lay outside this compass.

sentences.zh: 帝堯時，禹平水土，以爲九州。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yao, Yu pacified the waters and the land and thereby established the Nine Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yao, Yu brought floods and terrain under control and organized the realm into the Nine Provinces.

sentences.zh: 虞舜登庸，厥功彌劭，表提類而分區宇，判山河而考疆域，冀北創并部之名，燕齊起幽營之號，則書所謂肇十有二州，封十有二山者也。

translations.literal: When Shun of Yu ascended to employment, his achievements grew ever greater; he displayed categories and divided the realm, distinguished mountains and rivers and examined borders and domains, in the north of Ji created the name of the Bing region, in Yan and Qi raised the designations of You and Ying—this is what the documents call founding twelve provinces and enfeoffing twelve mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shun took power, his accomplishments deepened: he sorted kinds of terrain to partition the world, traced ranges and rivers to fix boundaries, coined the Bing administration north of Ji, and named the You and Ying regions out of Yan and Qi—exactly the twelve provinces and twelve sacred peaks spoken of in the classics.

sentences.zh: 夏功在于唐堯，殷因無所損益。

translations.literal: The Xia achievement lay with Tang Yao; Yin inherited it and made no additions or subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia order rested on the foundations Yao had laid; the Shang inherited that layout and left it unchanged.

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang and moved from Feng to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu overthrew Shang, the Zhou court shifted its seat from Feng to Hao.

sentences.zh: 至成王時，改作禹貢，徐梁入於青雍，冀野析於幽并。

translations.literal: By the time of King Cheng, the Yugong was revised: Xu and Liang were absorbed into Qing and Yong, and the Ji heartland was split between You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Cheng the Yugong scheme was redrawn: Xu and Liang were folded into Qing and Yong, while the old Ji plain was divided between the new You and Bing sectors.

sentences.zh: 職方掌天下之土，以周厥利；

translations.literal: The Office of Regions took charge of the soil of the world, in order to survey its advantages;
translations.idiomatic: The regional bureau mapped the empire’s lands and catalogued what each tract could yield;

sentences.zh: 保章辯九州之野，皆有分星。

translations.literal: The star-clerk distinguished the fields of the nine provinces; each had its allotted asterism.
translations.idiomatic: The astronomers correlated the nine provinces with the sky, assigning each region its own constellation.

sentences.zh: 東南曰揚州，正南曰荊州，河南曰豫州，正東曰青州，河東曰兗州，正西曰雍州，東北曰幽州，河內曰冀州，正北曰并州。

translations.literal: The southeast was called Yangzhou, the due south Jingzhou, south of the river Yuzhou, the due east Qingzhou, east of the river Yanzhou, the due west Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, within the river Jizhou, the due north Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou lay to the southeast, Jingzhou to the south, Yuzhou south of the Yellow River, Qingzhou to the east, Yanzhou east of the river, Yongzhou to the west, Youzhou to the northeast, Jizhou in the inner basin, and Bingzhou to the north.

sentences.zh: 始皇初并天下，懲{乂心}戰國，削罷列侯，分天下爲三十六郡。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor first united the realm, chastened by the lesson of the Warring States, he abolished the enfeoffed nobles and divided the world into thirty-six commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On first unifying China, the First Emperor, determined not to repeat the Warring States fragmentation, stripped the feudal lords of power and carved the empire into thirty-six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 〈三川、河東、南陽、南郡、九江、鄣郡、會稽、潁川、碭郡、泗水、薛郡、東郡、琅邪、齊郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西、遼東、代郡、鉅鹿、邯鄲、上黨、太原、雲中、九原、雁門、上郡、隴西、北地、漢中、巴郡、蜀郡、黔中、長沙，凡三十五郡，與內史爲三十六郡也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Sanshi, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, Xue, Dongjun, Langya, Qi, Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba, Shu, Qianzhong, and Changsha—thirty-five commanderies in all, which together with the metropolitan intendant made thirty-six commanderies.〉
translations.idiomatic: The gloss lists thirty-five outer commanderies—from Sanshi and Hedong through the northern and southern marches to Shu and Changsha—which, added to the capital intendant’s domain, made the famous thirty-six Qin commanderies.

sentences.zh: 於是興師踰江，平取百越，又置閩中、南海、桂林、象郡，凡四十郡，郡一守焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised armies, crossed the Yangtze, pacified and seized the Hundred Yue, and further established Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies—forty commanderies in all, each with one governor.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops south of the great river, subdued the Yue peoples, and added Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang, bringing the total to forty commanderies, each headed by a single appointed governor.

sentences.zh: 其地則西臨洮而北沙漠，東縈西帶，皆臨大海。

translations.literal: Its lands reached the Tao in the west and the desert in the north; ranges wound about it on the east and west like belts, and everywhere it fronted the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: The realm stretched west to the Tao River and north into the sands, girdled by mountains east and west, and everywhere opened toward the ocean.

sentences.zh: 漢祖龍興，革秦之弊，分內史爲三部，更置郡國二十有三，

translations.literal: When the Han progenitor rose as a dragon, he reformed Qin’s abuses, split the metropolitan intendant into three parts, and further established twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder, sweeping away Qin’s faults, divided the inner intendant into three jurisdictions and added twenty-three new commanderies and principalities,

sentences.zh: 〈桂陽、江夏、豫章、河內、魏郡、東海、楚國、平原、梁國、定襄、泰山、汝南、淮陽、千乘、東萊、燕國、清河、信都、常山、中山、渤海、廣漢、涿郡，合二十三也。

translations.literal: 〈Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Weijun, Donghai, the kingdom of Chu, Pingyuan, the kingdom of Liang, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, the kingdom of Yan, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, and Zhuo—twenty-three in all.〉
translations.idiomatic: The new jurisdictions were Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Weijun, Donghai, Chu, Pingyuan, Liang, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, and Zhuo—twenty-three units altogether.

sentences.zh: 三內史者，河上、渭南、中地也。

translations.literal: The three metropolitan intendants were Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi.
translations.idiomatic: The inner domain was split among the Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi intendancies.

sentences.zh: 地理志曰：高祖增二十六，武帝改河上、渭南、中地以爲京兆、馮翊、扶風，是爲三輔也。〉

translations.literal: The Treatise on Geography states: Gaozu added twenty-six; Wudi changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—this is the Three Adjuncts.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Han geography notes that Gaozu created twenty-six new units and that Emperor Wu reorganized Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—the region later called the Three Adjuncts.〉

translations.literal: Wendi added nine of them,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen added nine more domains,

sentences.zh: 〈廣平、城陽、淄川、濟南、膠西、膠東、河間、廬江、衡山，武帝改衡山曰「六安」。〉

translations.literal: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, and Hengshan—Wudi changed Hengshan to “Lu’an.”〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, and Hengshan—the last of which Emperor Wu renamed Lu’an.

translations.literal: Jingdi added four.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing added four more.

translations.literal: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: They were Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.

translations.literal: Xuandi changed Jibei to Dongping.〉
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan redesignated Jibei as Dongping.〉

sentences.zh: 武帝開越攘胡，初置十七，

translations.literal: Wudi opened Yue and repelled the Hu, first establishing seventeen,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu pushed into the south and drove back the steppe peoples, initially founding seventeen new commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡，平西南夷置牂柯、越巂、沈黎、汶山、犍爲、益州六郡，西置武都郡，又分立零陵郡，合十七郡。〉

translations.literal: 〈Nine commanderies on the southern coast—Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, and Dan’er—six commanderies set up after pacifying the southwestern Yi: Zangke, Yuexi, Shenli, Wenshan, Qianwei, and Yizhou; Wudu established in the west; and Lingling split off separately—seventeen commanderies in all.〉
translations.idiomatic: The note counts nine southern coastal commands, six created from the southwestern Yi campaign, the new Wudu outpost in the west, and a detached Lingling—seventeen additions in total.

translations.literal: Expanding territory and dividing borders, he further added fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: As borders widened, fourteen more commanderies were carved out.

sentences.zh: 〈弘農、臨淮、西河、朔方、酒泉、陳留、安定、天水、玄菟、樂浪、廣陵、敦煌、武威、張掖。〉

translations.literal: 〈Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, and Zhangye.〉
translations.idiomatic: They included Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, and Zhangye.

translations.literal: Zhaodi, with few undertakings, further added one.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao, undertaking little else, added one more commandery.

translations.literal: 〈Jincheng.〉
translations.idiomatic: That addition was Jincheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 至平帝元始二年，凡新置郡國七十有一，與秦四十，合一百一十有一。

translations.literal: By the second year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping, all newly established commanderies and kingdoms were seventy-one; together with Qin’s forty, they totaled one hundred eleven.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Ping’s Yuanshi 2, seventy-one new units had been created; added to the forty inherited from Qin, the empire counted one hundred eleven commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，又置徐州，復夏舊號，南置交阯，北有朔方，凡爲十三部。

translations.literal: Yong was changed to Liang, Liang was changed to Yi, Xu was further established, the old Xia designations were restored, Jiaozhi was set in the south, Shuofang existed in the north—in all thirteen divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yong became Liang, Liang became Yi, Xu was revived under its ancient name, Jiaozhi was organized in the south, Shuofang guarded the north, and the whole was grouped into thirteen inspectorates.

sentences.zh: 〈涼、益、荊、揚、青、豫、兗、徐、幽、并、冀十一州，交阯、朔方二刺史，合十三部。〉

translations.literal: 〈Eleven provinces—Liang, Yi, Jing, Yang, Qing, Yu, Yan, Xu, You, Bing, and Ji—plus two inspectors for Jiaozhi and Shuofang, thirteen divisions in all.〉
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen regional circuits comprised eleven provinces plus the two special inspectorates at Jiaozhi and Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 光武投戈之歲，在彫秏之辰，郡國蕭條，并省者八。

translations.literal: In the year Guangwu cast aside his weapons, at a time of exhaustion and waste, commanderies and kingdoms were desolate, and eight were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu laid down the sword amid a ruined realm, eight redundant commanderies were folded together or struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 〈城陽、淄川、高密、膠東、六安、真定、泗水、廣陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Lu’an, Zhending, Sishui, and Guangyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: The eight were Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Lu’an, Zhending, Sishui, and Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 建武十一年，省州牧，復爲刺史，員十三人，各掌一州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jianwu, provincial shepherds were abolished and replaced with regional inspectors; thirteen posts were set, each governing one province.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 11 the Eastern Han restored the old inspector system—thirteen officials, each supervising a single province.

translations.literal: Mingdi established one,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming added one commandery,

translations.literal: 〈Yongchang.〉
translations.idiomatic: That unit was Yongchang commandery.

translations.literal: Zhangdi established two,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang added two more,

translations.literal: 〈Rencheng and Wu commanderies.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Rencheng and Wu.

translations.literal: Under He and Shun there were alterations; the names involved were nine.
translations.idiomatic: During the He and Shun reigns nine further name changes or redesignations were recorded.

sentences.zh: 〈和置濟北、廣陽，順改淮陽爲陳，改楚爲彭城，濟東爲東平，臨淮爲下邳，千乘爲六安，信都爲安平，天水爲漢陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈He established Jibei and Guangyang; Shun changed Huaiyang to Chen, Chu to Pengcheng, Jidong to Dongping, Linhuai to Xiapi, Qiansheng to Lu’an, Xindu to Anping, and Tianshui to Hanyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: He’s additions were Jibei and Guangyang; Shun’s edicts renamed Huaiyang to Chen, Chu to Pengcheng, Jidong to Dongping, Linhuai to Xiapi, Qiansheng to Lu’an, Xindu to Anping, and Tianshui to Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 省朔方刺史，合之於司隸，凡十三部，

translations.literal: The Shuofang inspector was abolished and merged into the Sili intendant; in all there were thirteen divisions,
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang’s inspectorate was folded into the capital Sili circuit, leaving thirteen regional units,

sentences.zh: 〈其與西漢不同者，司隸校尉部郡治河南，朔方隸於并部。〉

translations.literal: 〈Where it differed from Western Han: the colonel of Sili governed commanderies with its seat in Henan, and Shuofang belonged to the Bing circuit.〉
translations.idiomatic: Unlike Western Han, the Sili colonel’s district was administered from Henan, while Shuofang answered to Bing.

translations.literal: And there were one hundred eight commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: The realm now comprised one hundred eight commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 〈省前漢八，分置五，改舊名七，因舊九十六，少前漢三也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Eight Western Han units were abolished, five were split off anew, seven old names were changed, ninety-six were retained from earlier arrangements—three fewer than Western Han.〉
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Western Han, eight jurisdictions disappeared, five were newly split, seven were renamed, ninety-six carried over unchanged—three fewer in total.

sentences.zh: 桓靈頗增於前，復置六郡。

translations.literal: Under Huan and Ling there were rather more additions than before, and six commanderies were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Huan and Ling emperors expanded the map again, reinstating six commanderies.

translations.literal: 〈Under Huan: Gaoyang, Gaoliang, and Boling;
translations.idiomatic: Huan’s additions were Gaoyang, Gaoliang, and Boling;

translations.literal: under Ling: Nan’an, Poyang, and Luling.〉
translations.idiomatic: Ling created Nan’an, Poyang, and Luling.〉

sentences.zh: 魏武定霸，三方鼎立，生靈版蕩，關洛荒蕪，所置者十二，

translations.literal: When Wei Wu secured hegemony, the three corners stood like a tripod; living souls were scattered and the heartland lay waste; twelve were established,
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao seized northern hegemony amid the tripartite standoff and a devastated Guanzhong and Luoyang plain, he created twelve new commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈新興、樂平、西平、新平、略陽、陰平、帶方、譙、樂陵、章武、南鄉、襄陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lüeyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, and Xiangyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lüeyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, and Xiangyang.

translations.literal: Seven were abolished,
translations.idiomatic: Seven older jurisdictions were eliminated,

sentences.zh: 〈上郡、朔方、五原、雲中、定襄、漁陽、廬江。〉

translations.literal: 〈Shang, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, and Lujiang.〉
translations.idiomatic: They included Shang, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, and Lujiang.

translations.literal: And Wendi established seven,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei then added seven more,

sentences.zh: 〈朝歌、陽平、弋陽、魏興、新城、義陽、[2]安豐。〉

translations.literal: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, Yiyang (弋陽), Weixing, Xincheng, Yiyang (義陽),[2] and Anfeng.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Zhaoge, Yangping, the eastern Yiyang commandery, Weixing, Xincheng, the southern Yiyang garrison,[2] and Anfeng.

translations.literal: Mingdi and the Young Emperor each added two,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming and the deposed Young Emperor each created two commanderies,

translations.literal: 〈Ming: Shangyong;
translations.idiomatic: Ming added Shangyong;

translations.literal: the Young Emperor: Pingyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: the Young Emperor added Pingyang.〉

translations.literal: Thus fifty-four Han commanderies were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Wei therefore controlled fifty-four former Han commanderies.

sentences.zh: 蜀先主於漢建安之間初置郡九，

translations.literal: Shu’s First Lord, between the Jian’an years of Han, first established nine commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Between the late Han Jian’an years, Liu Bei initially carved nine new commanderies out of Shu,

sentences.zh: 〈巴東、巴西、梓潼、江陽、汶山、漢嘉、朱提、宕渠、涪陵。〉

translations.literal: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, and Fuling.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, and Fuling.

translations.literal: The Later Lord added two,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan later added two more,

translations.literal: 〈Yunnan and Xinggu.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Yunnan and Xinggu.

translations.literal: Thus eleven Han commanderies were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Shu altogether held eleven former Han commanderies.

translations.literal: Wu’s ruler, the Great Emperor, first established five commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan initially founded five commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈臨賀、武昌、珠崖、新安、廬陵南部。〉

translations.literal: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin’an, and the southern part of Luling.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin’an, and southern Luling.

translations.literal: The Young Emperors and Emperor Jing each added four,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang and Sun Xiu each added four commanderies,

translations.literal: 〈The Young Emperor: Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, and Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang created Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, and Xiangdong;

sentences.zh: 景，天門、建安、建平、合浦北部。〉

translations.literal: Jing: Tianmen, Jian’an, Jianping, and northern Hepu.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu added Tianmen, Jian’an, Jianping, and northern Hepu.〉

translations.literal: The Marquis who Surrendered his Mandate also established twelve commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao likewise carved out twelve new commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈始安、始興、邵陵、安成、新昌、武平、九德、吳興、東陽、桂林、滎陽、宜都。〉

translations.literal: 〈Shi’an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Xingyang, and Yidu.〉
translations.idiomatic: They were Shi’an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Xingyang, and Yidu.

translations.literal: Thus eighteen Han commanderies were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ultimately governed eighteen former Han commanderies.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，既平孫氏，凡增置郡國二十有三，

translations.literal: In the first year of Taikang of Jin Wudi, once the Sun clan had been pacified, twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms were added in all,
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan crushed the Sun regime in Taikang 1, he reorganized the south with twenty-three new commanderies and kingdoms,

sentences.zh: 〈滎陽、上洛、頓丘、臨淮、東莞、襄城、汝陰、長廣、廣甯、昌黎、新野、隨郡、陰平、義陽、毗陵、宣城、南康、晉安、寧浦、始平、略陽、樂平、南平。〉

translations.literal: 〈Xingyang, Shangluo, Dunqiu, Linhuai, Dongguan, Xiangcheng, Ruyin, Changguang, Guangning, Changli, Xinye, Sui, Yinping, Yiyang, Piling, Xuancheng, Nankang, Jin’an, Ningpu, Shiping, Lüeyang, Leping, and Nanping.〉
translations.idiomatic: They included Xingyang, Shangluo, Dunqiu, Linhuai, Dongguan, Xiangcheng, Ruyin, Changguang, Guangning, Changli, Xinye, Sui, Yinping, Yiyang, Piling, Xuancheng, Nankang, Jin’an, Ningpu, Shiping, Lüeyang, Leping, and Nanping.

sentences.zh: 省司隸置司州，別立梁、秦、寧、平四州，仍吳之廣州，凡十九州，

translations.literal: Sili was abolished and Sizhou established; Liang, Qin, Ning, and Ping were separately founded; Wu’s Guangzhou was retained—in all nineteen provinces,
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court replaced the Han Sili circuit with a new Sizhou, added Liang, Qin, Ning, and Ping, kept Wu’s Guangzhou, and thus organized nineteen provinces,

sentences.zh: 〈司、冀、兗、豫、荊、徐、揚、青、幽、平、并、雍、涼、秦、梁、益、寧、交、廣州。〉

translations.literal: 〈Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, Xu, Yang, Qing, You, Ping, Bing, Yong, Liang (Hexi), Qin, Liang (upper Han), Yi, Ning, Jiao, and Guang provinces.〉
translations.idiomatic: The nineteen provinces were Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, Xu, Yang, Qing, You, Ping, Bing, Yong, the Hexi Liang circuit, Qin, the Hanzhong Liang circuit, Yi, Ning, Jiao, and Guang.

translations.literal: There were one hundred seventy-three commanderies and kingdoms,
translations.idiomatic: The empire now counted one hundred seventy-three commanderies and kingdoms,

sentences.zh: 〈仍吳所置二十五，仍蜀新置十一，仍魏所置二十一，仍漢舊九十三，置二十三。〉

translations.literal: 〈Twenty-five retained from Wu’s establishments, eleven retained from Shu’s new creations, twenty-one retained from Wei’s establishments, ninety-three inherited from old Han, and twenty-three newly founded.〉
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five came from Wu’s map, eleven from Shu’s additions, twenty-one from Wei’s roster, ninety-three survived unchanged from Han, and twenty-three were Jin’s own new units.

sentences.zh: 以爲冠帶之國，盡有殷周之土。

translations.literal: Thus as a girdled-and-capped state it fully possessed the soil of Yin and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a civilized empire at the heart of the world, Jin encompassed all the lands once ruled by Shang and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 若乃敦龐於天地之始，昭晰於犧農之世，用長黎元，未爭疆埸。

translations.literal: As for being vast at the beginning of Heaven and Earth, being clear in the age of Xi and Nong, thereby nurturing the black-haired people, they did not yet contend over borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the primordial vastness before history, when Fuxi and Shennong brought clarity to human life, rulers simply nurtured their people and knew nothing of fighting over frontiers.

sentences.zh: 而玉環楛矢，夷裘風駕，南翬表貺，東風入律，光乎上德，奚遠弗臻。

translations.literal: Yet jade rings and arrow-shafts of mulberry, barbarian furs and wind-borne chariots, southern pheasant-banners displaying tribute, eastern winds entering the pitch-pipes—such radiance of supreme virtue: what distant place did it not reach?
translations.idiomatic: Jade tokens and tribute arrows, furs borne in from the steppes, southern envoys presenting their gifts, spring winds harmonizing with the pitch-pipes—all testified to a virtue so brilliant that no corner of the world lay beyond its reach.

sentences.zh: 然則星象麗天，山河紀地，端掖裁其弘敞，崤函判其都邑，仰觀俯察，萬物攸歸。

translations.literal: Thus star patterns adorn Heaven, mountains and rivers record Earth; the two palace wings measure its breadth, Xiao and Han mark off its capitals; looking up and looking down, the myriad things have their place.
translations.idiomatic: Constellations pattern the sky while rivers and mountains inscribe the earth; the twin palace flanks frame the capital’s grandeur, the Xiao and Han passes define its seat of power—gazing upward and downward, every creature finds its allotted home.

sentences.zh: 是以洛沚咸陽，宛然秦漢，晉濱河西，同知堯禹，于茲新邑，宅是鎬京，五尺童子皆能口誦者，史官弗之書也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Luo basin and Xianyang, clearly Qin and Han; Jin along the west of the river, equally known to Yao and Yu; here in this new city, dwelling in this Hao capital—what even a five-foot child can recite from memory, the scribes do not write down.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows how the Luo heartland and Xianyang echo Qin and Han, how the Jin domain along the western river recalls the age of Yao and Yu, and how this new capital claims the mantle of old Hao—truths so familiar that every child repeats them, which is why the official histories pass them over in silence.

sentences.zh: 昔庖犧氏生於成紀，而爲天子，都於陳。

translations.literal: Formerly the Paoxi clan was born at Chengji and became Son of Heaven, with its capital at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Legend places the birth of Fuxi’s clan at Chengji; as sovereigns they ruled from Chen.

sentences.zh: 神農氏都陳，而別營于曲阜。

translations.literal: The Shennong clan had its capital at Chen, but separately built a camp at Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Shennong ruled from Chen yet maintained another center at Qufu.

sentences.zh: 黃帝生於壽丘，而都於涿鹿。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor was born at Shouqiu and had his capital at Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor was born on Mount Shouqiu and established his capital at Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 少昊始自窮桑，而遷都曲阜。

translations.literal: Shaohao began from Qiongsang and moved the capital to Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao rose from Qiongsang and later shifted his seat to Qufu.

sentences.zh: 顓頊始自窮桑，而徙邑商丘。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu began from Qiongsang and moved the town to Shangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu likewise started from Qiongsang before relocating his capital to Shangqiu.

translations.literal: Gaoxin took the title and built the capital at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ku assumed the throne and founded his capital at Bo.

sentences.zh: 孫卿子曰：「不登高山，不知天之高；

translations.literal: Master Xun said: “If one does not climb a high mountain, one does not know how high Heaven is;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Qing said, “Without climbing a lofty peak, you cannot grasp how high the sky reaches;

sentences.zh: 不臨深谿，不知地之厚也。

translations.literal: If one does not stand beside a deep ravine, one does not know how thick the earth is.
translations.idiomatic: If you never stand above a deep gorge, you have no measure of how thick the earth runs.

sentences.zh: 」大哉坤象，萬物資生，載崑華而不墜，傾河海而寧泄。

translations.literal: The passage then exclaims: how great is the image of Kun—the myriad things receive life from it; it supports Kunlun and Mount Hua without collapsing, and channels the rivers and seas toward the deeps without being exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative then turns to praise the earth’s power: every living thing draws sustenance from it, it can bear up Kunlun and Mount Hua without failing, and it can pour the great rivers and oceans toward the abyss without ever running dry.

sentences.zh: 考卜惟王，乘飛駐軫，睨𡹮山而鐫勒，覽曾城以爲玩。

translations.literal: Divining, they chose the king; riding flying chariots they halted the carriage shafts; gazing toward the mountains they carved inscriptions, viewing layered capitals they took them for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns divined their mandate, raced in swift chariots, paused to carve boastful inscriptions on sacred peaks, and toured tiered capitals as though they were pleasure grounds.

sentences.zh: 時逢稽浸，道接陵夷，平王東遷，星離豆剖，當塗馭宇，瓜分鼎立。

translations.literal: Times met with prolonged disaster, the Way slid into decline, King Ping moved the capital east, the realm scattered like stars and split like pods, and when the House of Cao grasped the mandate the empire was carved apart like a melon and balanced like rival tripods.
translations.idiomatic: Calamity dragged on, royal virtue ebbed, King Ping abandoned the west, and the world flew apart; then the Caos seized the throne and the land broke into contending thirds, each claiming a share of the ancient cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝接千祀之餘，當八堯之禪，先王桑梓，罄宇來歸，斯固可得而言者矣。

translations.literal: Our dynastic founder, Emperor Wu, inherited the accumulated mandate of many generations, received the abdicated throne in the ancient model of Yao and Shun, and saw the former kings’ homelands and the whole realm submit—this is indeed something that can be told.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, the dynastic founder, picked up a mandate long in the making, accepted Wei’s abdication as Yao once yielded to Shun, and watched the old royal heartlands and every quarter of the realm come over to him—events that plainly deserve narration.

sentences.zh: 惠皇不虞，中州盡棄，永嘉南度，綸行建鄴，九分天下而有二焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui met unexpected calamity, the Central Plain was entirely lost, in the Yongjia era the court crossed south, the imperial progress went to Jianye, and of nine parts of the realm they held but two.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui fell victim to coup and war, the heartland was abandoned; with the Yongjia exodus the court crossed the Yangtze and the imperial train made Jianye its seat, so that Jin retained only two of the nine traditional divisions of the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔大禹觀於濁河而受綠字，寰瀛之內可得而言也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yu the Great gazed upon the muddy Yellow River and received the green writing; within the ring of the seas it can therefore be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu the Great stood by the turbid Yellow River and received the river chart, he gained a model by which the whole world within the four seas could be described.

translations.literal: Heaven has the seven stars; Earth has the seven markers;
translations.idiomatic: Just as the sky is marked by seven principal stars, so the earth is marked by seven frontier belts;

translations.literal: Heaven has four sustaining cords (weft/bindings); earth has four great draining channels.
translations.idiomatic: The sky is hung on four cosmic stays, and the land is gouged by four mighty watercourses that carry the flood away.

translations.literal: Outside the eight cords of the world, they are called the eight extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the encircling girdle that ropes in the known world lie the eight outermost reaches.

sentences.zh: 地不足東南，天不足西北。

translations.literal: Earth falls short toward the southeast; heaven falls short toward the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The ground gives way to the southeast, while the empyrean gapes widest toward the northwest.

sentences.zh: 八極之廣，東西二億三萬一千三百里，南北二億三萬一千三百里。

translations.literal: The breadth of the eight extremities: east and west, two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li; north and south, likewise two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern pole to the western spans two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li—and the same measure runs from south to north.

sentences.zh: 自地至天，半八極之數，自下亦如之。

translations.literal: From earth to heaven is half the tally of the eight extremities; from below upward it is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The vault above measured half the span of the Eight Poles, and the same depth echoed below.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝令豎亥步自東極，至于西極，五億十萬九千八百八步。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor ordered Shu Hai to pace from the eastern extremity to the western extremity: five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight paces.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yellow Emperor bade Shu Hai stride from sunrise to sunset; the tally came to five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight measured paces.

sentences.zh: 史臣案，凡周天積百七萬九百一十三里，徑三十五萬六千九百七十里。

translations.literal: The court historiographers ascertain: in all the circumference of heaven totals one million seventy thousand nine hundred thirteen li; the diameter is three hundred fifty-six thousand nine hundred seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: Court mathematicians reckoned heaven's circuit at 1,070,913 li and its diameter at 356,970 li.

sentences.zh: 所謂南北爲經，東西爲緯。

translations.literal: That which is called: north-south as warp, east-west as weft.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by naming north-south the warp and east-west the weft.

sentences.zh: 天有十二次，日月之所躔；

translations.literal: Heaven has twelve celestial lodges; they are where the sun and moon tread their circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Twelve lunar lodges score the sky—the highway of sun and moon;

sentences.zh: 地有十二辰，王侯之所國也。

translations.literal: earth has twelve earthly branches; they are where kings and marquises establish states.
translations.idiomatic: twelve earthly divisions underpin the map where lords and princes plant their altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 或因生得姓，因功命土，祁、酉、燕、齊，在乎茲域。

translations.literal: Some by birth obtain surnames, by merit receive land; Qi, You, Yan, and Qi lie within this region.
translations.idiomatic: Some clans took names from ancestral seats, others earned fiefs for deeds done—and the old domains of Qi, You, Yan, and Qi all fall inside these bounds.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝旁行天下，方制萬里，得百里之國萬區，則《周易》所謂「首出庶物，萬國咸寧」者也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor traveled the realm in all directions, regulated a square of ten thousand li, and obtained ten thousand regions of hundred-li states—this is what the Zhou Yi calls "first emerging among the myriad things; the myriad states all attain tranquility."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor quartered the realm, squared a domain ten thousand li on a side, and carved it into ten thousand hundred-li polities—the very epoch the Book of Changes extols when it says, "He who rises first above the throng brings every kingdom to rest."

sentences.zh: 昔在帝堯，協和萬邦，制八家爲鄰，三鄰爲朋，三朋爲里，五里爲邑，十邑爲都，十都爲師，州十有二師焉。

translations.literal: Formerly under Emperor Yao he harmonized the myriad states; he regulated: eight households form a neighborhood, three neighborhoods form a peng, three peng form a li, five li form a yi, ten yi form a du, ten du form a shi, and a province has twelve shi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao the countries learned concord, and government knit tight: eight families made a street, three streets a cluster, three clusters a ward, five wards a market town, ten such towns a greater burgh, ten burghs a canton, and twelve cantons stitched one province.

sentences.zh: 夏后氏東漸于海，西被于流沙，南浮于江，而朔南暨聲教，窮豎亥所步，莫不率俾，會群臣於塗山，執玉帛者萬國。

translations.literal: The house of Xia eastward reached to the sea, westward extended to the flowing sands, southward floated on the Jiang; north and south likewise were united by culture and teaching, exhausting where Shu Hai had paced; none failed to follow and obey; they assembled the host of lords at Tu Shan; those bearing jade and silk were ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia stretched east until the tide foamed at their feet, west to the shifting sands, south along the great rivers, until their transforming influence ran from pole to pole as far as Shu Hai had ever measured; none refused homage. At Mount Tu they gathered the lords, and ten thousand courts arrived with jade disks and silk.

sentences.zh: 於是九州之內，作爲五服。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the nine provinces they established the five domains (fu).
translations.idiomatic: Within the Nine Provinces they layered five concentric belts of fealty.

sentences.zh: 天子之國，內五百里甸服，百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's state: the inner five hundred li is the royal domain; at one hundred li tribute is delivered as bound sheaves in the husk; at two hundred li sickle-cut ears; at three hundred li straw and corvée service; at four hundred li millet; at five hundred li rice.
translations.idiomatic: Around the capital ran five hundred li of royal fields: the inner ring sent whole stalks bundled, the next matured heads, the third straw and labor, the fourth threshed grain, the outermost polished rice for the palace kettle.

sentences.zh: 甸服外五百里侯服，百里采，二百里任，三百里候。

translations.literal: Outside the royal domain, five hundred li of marquis-domain: one hundred li of estates, two hundred li of appointments, three hundred li of garrison/watch.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that stretched another five hundred li of baronial land: the first hundred fed royal manors, the next two hundred supplied ministers of trust, the outer three hundred patrolled the marches.

sentences.zh: 侯服外五百里綏服，三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。

translations.literal: Outside the marquis-domain, five hundred li of pacification-domain: three hundred li for adjusting civil teaching and rites, two hundred li for vigorous martial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five hundred li meant to "soothe": three hundred for schools and rites, two hundred bristling with spears that guarded the cordon.

sentences.zh: 綏服外五百里要服，三百里夷，二百里蔡。

translations.literal: Outside the pacification-domain, five hundred li of binding-domain: three hundred li of outer Yi, two hundred li of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the pacified belt lay five hundred li of "treaty" ground—three hundred li of loosely ruled bordermen, two hundred more under banishment law.

sentences.zh: 要服外五百里荒服，三百里蠻，二百里流。

translations.literal: Outside the binding-domain, five hundred li of wild-domain: three hundred li of Man, two hundred li of exile-flow.
translations.idiomatic: The rim was five hundred li of wilderness—three hundred left to rough hill tribes, two hundred reserved for the river of banishment.

sentences.zh: 訖于四海，弼成五服，五服至于五千里。

translations.literal: Reaching to the four seas, they assisted in completing the five domains; the five domains extend to five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The pattern ran to the four seas, the five girdles locked in place, a full five thousand li from throne to tide-line.

translations.literal: Midway Xia's virtue withered; it encountered the disorder of Youqiong.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway through their age the Xia lost heart, and the realm reeled beneath Youqiong's revolt.

translations.literal: Shaokang raised a restoration; he did not lose the old inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Shaokang rallied the line and never surrendered the ancestral cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 自孔甲之後，以至于桀，諸侯相兼，其能存者三千餘國，方於塗山，十損其七矣。

translations.literal: From Kong Jia onward, down to Jie, the feudal lords mutually annexed; those able to survive numbered a bit more than three thousand states; compared to Mount Tu, ten lost seven.
translations.idiomatic: From Kong Jia to tyrant Jie the lords devoured one another until barely three thousand states remained—seven in ten had vanished since the great conference at Mount Tu.

sentences.zh: 成湯敗桀於焦，遷鼎於亳，伊摯、仲虺之徒，大明憲典。

translations.literal: Cheng Tang defeated Jie at Jiao, moved the cauldrons to Bo; men such as Yi Zhi and Zhong Hui greatly clarified statutes and models.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tang broke Jie at Jiao and carried the tripods to Bo; ministers like Yi Yin and Zhong Hui lit clear lamps of law and precedent.

sentences.zh: 王者之制爵祿，公侯伯子男凡五等。

translations.literal: The king's system of enfeoffing ranks and salaries: duke, marquis, earl, viscount, baron—in all five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Royal custom fixed five noble ranks—from duke down to baron—each with its stipend.

sentences.zh: 天子之田方千里，公侯田方百里，伯七十里，子男五十里。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's field is a square of a thousand li; duke and marquis, a square of a hundred li; earl, seventy li; viscount and baron, fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: The king measured a thousand li square; dukes and marquises a hundred, earls seventy, viscounts and barons a bare fifty on a side.

sentences.zh: 不能五十里者，不達於天子，附於諸侯，曰附庸。

translations.literal: Those unable to reach fifty li do not communicate directly with the Son of Heaven; they attach to feudal lords; they are called dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Polities shy of fifty li could not seek audience alone; they hung on greater lords as client domains.

sentences.zh: 凡四海之內九州，州方千里。

translations.literal: In all, within the four seas are nine provinces; each province is a square of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas lay nine provinces, each a thousand-li square on the chart.

sentences.zh: 州建百里之國三十，七十里之國六十，五十里之國百有二十，凡二百一十國。

translations.literal: In a province are established thirty states of a hundred li, sixty states of seventy li, one hundred twenty states of fifty li—in all two hundred ten states.
translations.idiomatic: Each province raised thirty great hundred-li realms, sixty middling seventy-li counties, and a hundred twenty small fifty-li cells—two hundred ten banners in all.

sentences.zh: 名山大澤不以封，其餘以爲附庸間田。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not used for enfeoffment; the remainder becomes dependencies and interstitial fields.
translations.idiomatic: Crown peaks and imperial bogs never left the king's ledger; leftover patches became vassal pockets and buffer strips.

translations.literal: Eight provinces—each province two hundred ten states.
translations.idiomatic: Eight of the nine provinces repeated that pattern—two hundred ten states apiece.

sentences.zh: 天子之縣內，百里之國九，七十里之國二十有一，五十里之國六十有三，凡九十三國。

translations.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's direct counties: nine states of a hundred li, twenty-one states of seventy li, sixty-three states of fifty li—in all ninety-three states.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the royal demesne itself stood nine hundred-li seats, twenty-one seventy-li manors, and sixty-three fifty-li plots—ninety-three realms devoted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 名山大澤不以班，其餘以祿士，以爲間田。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not parceled out in enfeoffment; the remainder is used to salary officers and becomes interstitial fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred heights and royal marshes were never fiefed away; the scraps paid stipendiary officials and plugged holes between grants.

sentences.zh: 凡九州，千七百七十三國。

translations.literal: In all the nine provinces: one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Nine Provinces the tallies listed one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.

sentences.zh: 天子之元士，諸侯之附庸，不與。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's chief knights and the feudal lords' dependencies are not included.
translations.idiomatic: The count omits the king's senior householders and the petty clients of great barons.

sentences.zh: 天子百里之內以供官，千里之內以爲御，千里之外設方伯。

translations.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's hundred li, for supplying officials; within a thousand li, for court provision; beyond a thousand li, regional hegemons are appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The inner hundred li fed the bureaucracy, the thousand li stocked palace service, and beyond that the king set regional elders to rule in his stead.

translations.literal: Five states form a dependency-group; a dependency-group has a chief.
translations.idiomatic: Five states formed a dependency cluster led by a chief.

translations.literal: Ten states form a chain; a chain has a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ten states formed a league placed under a captain.

translations.literal: Thirty states form a corps; a corps has a director.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty states formed a corps overseen by a senior marshal.

sentences.zh: 二百一十國以爲州，州有伯。

translations.literal: Two hundred ten states form a province; a province has a bo.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred ten states formed a province ruled by a regional elder.

sentences.zh: 八州，八伯，五十六正，百六十八帥，三百三十六長。

translations.literal: Eight provinces: eight bo, fifty-six directors, one hundred sixty-eight commanders, three hundred thirty-six chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Eight provinces meant eight great lords, fifty-six marshals, one hundred sixty-eight captains, and three hundred thirty-six village heads.

sentences.zh: 八伯各以其屬屬於天子之老二人，分天下爲左右，曰二伯。

translations.literal: Each of the eight bo with his dependents attaches to two elders of the Son of Heaven; they divide the realm into left and right, called the two bo.
translations.idiomatic: Each provincial lord knelt to one of the king's two senior regents, splitting the world into eastern and western halves—the Two Chiefs of high Zhou.

sentences.zh: 千里之內曰甸，千里之外曰采，曰流。

translations.literal: Within a thousand li is called dian; beyond a thousand li is called cai and liu.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the thousand-li cordon lay the royal hearths; outside stretched ministerial estates and the flowing lands of exile.

sentences.zh: 天子使其大夫爲三監，監於方伯之國，國三人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven causes his great officers to be triple overseers; they oversee in the regional hegemons' states; three men per state.
translations.idiomatic: The king posted three-man inspectorates in every regional capital to eye the barons for him.

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's counties: inwardly, they are stipendiary fiefs for feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Domains hugging the throne were stipendiary grants to great lords.

translations.literal: Outwardly, they are inheriting lineages of feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Those farther out settled into noble lines handed down through inheritance.

sentences.zh: 武王歸豐，監於二代，設爵惟五，分土惟三。

translations.literal: King Wu returned to Feng, examined the two dynasties, established ranks only five, divided land only three grades.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu withdrew to Feng, studied Xia and Shang, fixed five noble rows, and sorted fief size into three steps.

sentences.zh: 封同姓五十餘國，周公、康叔建於魯衛，各數百里。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed kinsmen fifty-odd states; the Duke of Zhou and Kang Shu were established at Lu and Wei, each several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He planted more than fifty Zhou princes across the map—the Duke of Zhou at Lu, Kang Shu at Wei—each commanding several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 太公封於齊，表東海者也。

translations.literal: Grand Duke Tai was enfeoffed at Qi—he who screens the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Gong took Qi as his shield against the eastern tide.

sentences.zh: 凡一千八百國，布列於五千里內。

translations.literal: In all one thousand eight hundred states, arrayed within five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen hundred realms checkered the five-thousand-li heartland.

sentences.zh: 而太昊、黃帝之後，唐虞侯伯猶存。

translations.literal: Moreover descendants of Taihao and the Yellow Emperor—Tang-Yao era marquises and earls—still survived.
translations.idiomatic: Lines sprung from Taihao and the Yellow Emperor, marquises who remembered Yao and Shun, still clung to titles in that new Zhou dawn.

sentences.zh: 大司徒以諸公之地封疆方五百里，其食者半；

translations.literal: The grand steward: the lands of the dukes have boundaries a square of five hundred li; of it half provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education carved dukes five hundred li square but let them tax only half the soil;

sentences.zh: 諸侯之地方四百里，其食者參之一；

translations.literal: The lands of marquises are four hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: marquises held four hundred li yet drew a third to their kitchens;

sentences.zh: 諸伯之地方三百里，其食者參之一；

translations.literal: The lands of earls are three hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: earls kept three hundred li with the same third rule;

sentences.zh: 諸子之地方二百里，其食者四之一；

translations.literal: The lands of viscounts are two hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: viscounts two hundred li but spent only a quarter;

sentences.zh: 諸男之地方百里，其食者四之一。

translations.literal: The lands of barons are a hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: barons a bare hundred li yet owned a quarter of the yield.

sentences.zh: 不易之地家百畝，一易之地家二百畝，再易之地家三百畝。

translations.literal: On land that does not rotate, a household receives a hundred mu; on land rotated once, two hundred mu; on land rotated twice, three hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: Permanent fields granted a household a hundred mu, once-fallow soil two hundred, and thrice-tired ground three hundred so the tax base stayed even.

translations.literal: Five households form a bi; they are caused mutually to guarantee.
translations.idiomatic: Five families swore mutual bail;

translations.literal: Five bi form a lü; they are caused mutually to shelter.
translations.idiomatic: five such rings a lane that housed the homeless;

translations.literal: Four lü form a zu; they are caused mutually to bury.
translations.idiomatic: four lanes a clan burying its dead together;

translations.literal: Five zu form a dang; they are caused mutually to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: five clans a company that rushed to fires and raids;

translations.literal: Five dang form a zhou; they are caused mutually to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: five companies a canton pooling famine grain;

translations.literal: Five zhou form a xiang; they are caused mutually to observe guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: five cantons a countryside whose elders still bowed in guest-rite.

sentences.zh: 小司徒以五人爲伍，五伍爲兩，四兩爲卒，五卒爲旅，五旅爲師，五師爲軍。

translations.literal: The lesser steward: by five men a squad, five squads a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a division, five divisions an army.
translations.idiomatic: The junior steward stacked squads: five men a file, five files a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a host, five hosts the full army.

sentences.zh: 以起軍旅，以作田役，以比追胥，以令貢賦。

translations.literal: By this raise armies, perform field labor and corvée, compare pursuit and night patrol, order tribute and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Those ladders raised campaigns, drafted ditch gangs, mustered night watchmen, and split the grain and corvée rolls.

sentences.zh: 乃經土地而井牧其田野，九夫爲井，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘，四丘爲甸，四甸爲縣，四縣爲都。

translations.literal: Then they surveyed land and well-and-pastured the fields and wilds: nine husbands a well, four wells a settlement, four settlements a mound, four mounds a dian, four dian a county, four counties a metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: Surveyors laid the well-net: nine farmers to a well, four wells a hamlet, four hamlets a hill-girdle, four hill-girdles a parcel, four parcels a county, four counties a great city.

sentences.zh: 遺人則十里有廬，廬有飲食。

translations.literal: The supply officer: then every ten li has a hut; the hut has drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers found a lodge every ten li with water and a warm bowl.

sentences.zh: 三十里有宿，宿有路室，路室有委。

translations.literal: Every thirty li has a lodging; the lodging has roadside chambers; the roadside chambers have stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Every thirty li brought a full station, roadside cells, and stacked grain.

sentences.zh: 五十里有市，市有候，候有館，館有積。

translations.literal: Every fifty li has a market; the market has a post; the post has a lodge; the lodge has accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: Every fifty li markets bustled with guard posts, guest halls, and piled stores.

sentences.zh: 遂人則五家爲鄰，五鄰爲里，四里爲酇，五酇爲鄙，五鄙爲縣，五縣爲遂。

translations.literal: The field officer: five households form lin, five lin a li, four li a zan, five zan a bi, five bi a county, five counties a sui.
translations.idiomatic: Rural marshals wove five homes into a lane, five lanes a hamlet, four hamlets a township, five townships a patch, five patches a county, five counties a sui belt.

sentences.zh: 大司馬以九畿之籍，施邦國之政。

translations.literal: The grand marshal, by the registers of the nine ji, applies governance to the states.
translations.idiomatic: The war minister read the nine belts girding Wangcheng and from them spun every lord's marching orders.

sentences.zh: 方千里曰國畿，其外方五百里曰侯畿，又其外方五百里曰甸畿，又其外方五百里曰男畿，又其外方五百里曰采畿，又其外方五百里曰衛畿，又其外方五百里曰蠻畿，又其外方五百里曰夷畿，又其外方五百里曰鎮畿，又其外方五百里曰藩畿。

translations.literal: A square of a thousand li is called the royal ji; its outer square of five hundred li is the marquis ji; again outside five hundred li is the dian ji; again outside five hundred li is the male-rank ji; again outside five hundred li is the stipend ji; again outside five hundred li is the guard ji; again outside five hundred li is the man ji; again outside five hundred li is the yi ji; again outside five hundred li is the garrison ji; again outside five hundred li is the vassal-screen ji.
translations.idiomatic: The capital sat in a thousand-li square; then nine half-thousand-li rings unrolled—baronial fields, royal estates, male fiefs, salary lands, guard strips, southern wilds, eastern wilds, garrison marches, and a final curtain of outer vassals.

translations.literal: 〈Ji means the field limit.
translations.idiomatic: The marginal note explains that ji denotes the border of taxable fields.

sentences.zh: 自王城以外，面五千里爲界，有分限者九也。〉

translations.literal: From outside the royal city, on each face five thousand li is the boundary; there are nine division-limits.〉
translations.idiomatic: It adds that from the royal walls each quarter runs five thousand li, ringed by nine stepped partitions.

sentences.zh: 于時治致太平，政稱刑措，民口千三百七十一萬四千九百三十三，蓋周之盛者也。

translations.literal: At that time rule attained the Great Peace, government was called punishments set aside, the people's mouths numbered thirteen million seven hundred fourteen thousand nine hundred thirty-three—this was the height of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That age ripened into the Great Peace, the racks stood empty, and the census inked 13,714,933 names—a Zhou summer at flood tide.

sentences.zh: 其衰也，則禮樂征伐出自諸侯，強吞弱而眾暴寡。

translations.literal: In its decline, then rites, music, expeditions, and punitive attacks issued from the feudal lords; the strong swallowed the weak and the many tyrannized the few.
translations.idiomatic: When it rotted, drums and odes marched under barons' banners, strong states swallowed weak neighbors, and packs harried the lone.

sentences.zh: 春秋之初，尚有千二百國，迄獲麟之末，二百四十二年，弒君三十六，亡國五十二，諸侯奔走不得保其社稷者不可勝數，而見於春秋經傳者百有七十國焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Spring and Autumn there were still one thousand two hundred states; down to the end of capturing the unicorn, two hundred forty-two years, regicide of lords thirty-six, perished states fifty-two, feudal lords fleeing unable to preserve their altars—uncountable; yet those appearing in the Spring and Autumn classic and commentaries numbered one hundred seventy states.
translations.idiomatic: Early Spring and Autumn still counted twelve hundred flags; by the day Confucius penned the unicorn's close—two hundred forty-two bloodied years—thirty-six kings had been knifed, fifty-two realms snuffed, and numberless lords fled ruined shrines, though the classic and its gloss remember only one hundred seventy names.

translations.literal: One hundred thirty-nine know where they dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thirty-nine of them still have identifiable capitals on the map.

sentences.zh: 〈魯、邾、鄭、宋、紀、衛、西虢、莒、齊、陳、杞、蔡、邢、郕、晉、薛、許、鄧、秦、曹、楚、隨、黃、梁、虞、鄖、小邾、徐、燕、鄀、麋、舒、庸、郯、萊、吳、越、有窮、三苗、瓜州、有虞、東虢、共、宿、申、夷、向、南燕、滕、凡、戴、息、郜、芮、魏、淳于、穀、巴、州、蓼、羅、賴、牟、葛、譚、蕭、遂、滑、權、鄣、霍、耿、江、冀、弦、道、柏、微、鄫、厲、項、密、任、須句、顓臾、頓、管、雍、畢、豐、邘、應、蔣、茅、胙、夔、介、焦、沈、六、巢、根牟、唐、黎、郇瑕、寒、有鬲、斟灌、斟尋、過、有過、戈、偪陽、邿、鑄、豕韋、唐杜、楊、豳、鄶、觀、扈、邳、胡、黎、大庭、駘、岐、邶、鍾吾、蒲姑、昆吾、房、密須、甲父、鄅、桐、亳、韓、趙。〉

translations.literal: (Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Ji, Wei, Western Guo, Ju, Qi, Chen, Qi, Cai, Xing, Cheng, Jin, Xue, Xu, Deng, Qin, Cao, Chu, Sui, Huang, Liang, Yu, Yun, Lesser Zhu, Xu, Yan, Ruo, Mi, Shu, Yong, Tan, Lai, Wu, Yue, Youqiong, Sanmiao, Guazhou, You Yu, Eastern Guo, Gong, Su, Shen, Yi, Xiang, Southern Yan, Teng, Fan, Dai, Xi, Gao, Rui, Wei, Chunyu, Gu, Ba, Zhou, Liao, Luo, Lai, Mou, Ge, Tan, Xiao, Sui, Hua, Quan, Zhang, Huo, Geng, Jiang, Ji, Xian, Dao, Bo, Wei, Zeng, Li, Xiang, Mi, Ren, Xuqu, Zhuanyu, Dun, Guan, Yong, Bi, Feng, Yu, Ying, Jiang, Mao, Zuo, Kui, Jie, Jiao, Shen, Liu, Chao, Genmou, Tang, Li, Xunxia, Han, Youge, Zhuguan, Zhunxun, Guo, Youguo, Ge, Biyang, Shi, Zhu, Shangwei, Tang Du, Yang, Bin, Kuai, Guan, Hu, Li, Danting, Tai, Qi, Bei, Zhongwu, Pugu, Kunwu, Fang, Mixu, Jiafu, Yu, Tong, Bo, Han, Zhao.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss strings together more than a hundred collateral polities—from Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Ji, Wei, Western Guo, Ju, Qi, Chen, Qi (of the east), Cai, Xing, Cheng, Jin, Xue, Xu, Deng, Qin, Cao, Chu, Sui, Huang, Liang, Yu, Yun, Lesser Zhu, Xu, Yan, Ruo, Mi, Shu, Yong, Tan, Lai, Wu, and Yue through Youqiong, Sanmiao, Guazhou, You Yu, Eastern Guo, Gong, Su, Shen, Yi, Xiang, Southern Yan, Teng, Fan, Dai, Xi, Gao, Rui, Wei, Chunyu, Gu, Ba, Zhou, Liao, Luo, Lai, Mou, Ge, Tan, Xiao, Sui, Hua, Quan, Zhang, Huo, Geng, Jiang, Ji, Xian, Dao, Bo, Wei, Zeng, Li, Xiang, Mi, Ren, Xuqu, Zhuanyu, Dun, Guan, Yong, Bi, Feng, Yu, Ying, Jiang, Mao, Zuo, Kui, Jie, Jiao, Shen, Liu, Chao, Genmou, Tang, Li, Xunxia, Han, Youge, Zhuguan, Zhunxun, Guo, Youguo, Ge, Biyang, Shi, Zhu, Shangwei, Tang Du, Yang, Bin, Kuai, Guan, Hu, Li, Danting, Tai, Qi, Bei, Zhongwu, Pugu, Kunwu, Fang, Mixu, Jiafu, Yu, Tong, Bo, Han, and Zhao—whose lost seats later scholars can still roughly place from the classics and commentaries.

translations.literal: Thirty-one states utterly lost their locations.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one others vanished so completely that their very sites are forgotten.

sentences.zh: 〈祭、極、荀、賈、貳、軫、絞、於餘丘、陽、箕、英氏、毛、聃、莘、偪、封父、仍、有仍、崇、鄟、庸、姺、奄、商奄、褒姒、蓐、有緡、闕鞏、飂、鬷、窮桑。〉

translations.literal: (Zhai, Ji, Xun, Jia, Er, Zhen, Jiao, Yuyuqiu, Yang, Ji, Ying, Mao, Dan, Shen, Bi, Fengfu, Reng, Youreng, Chong, Tuan, Yong, Shen, Yan, Shangyan, Baosi, Ru, Youmin, Quegong, Liu, Zong, Qiongsang.)
translations.idiomatic: The note preserves a further stratum of half-legendary seats—Zhai, Ji, Xun, Jia, Er, Zhen, Jiao, Yuyuqiu, Yang, Ji, Ying, Mao, Dan, Shen, Bi, Fengfu, Reng, Youreng, Chong, Tuan, Yong, Shen, Yan, Shangyan, Baosi, Ru, Youmin, Quegong, Liu, Zong, and Qiongsang—names that survive now chiefly as pale traces in exegetical literature.

translations.literal: The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are not among these.
translations.idiomatic: Southern, eastern, western, and northern tribes were never part of that roll.

translations.literal: The Five Hegemons rose in succession; they oversaw their covenants and assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Five overlords rose in turn to chair the league altars and stamp clan oaths.

sentences.zh: 陵夷至于戰國，遂有七王，

translations.literal: Declining further, it reached the Warring States; thereupon there were seven kings,
translations.idiomatic: The slide ran on into the Warring States, and seven crowned powers shouldered the world—

translations.literal: (Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, Chu.)
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, and Chu.

sentences.zh: 又有宋、衛、中山，不斷如綫，如三晉篡奪，亦稱孤也。

translations.literal: Moreover there were Song, Wei, and Zhongshan, unbroken like a thread; as for the usurpations of the three Jin, they also called themselves orphaned rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Wei, and Zhongshan still hung by a thread, while the breakaway triplets of Jin stole the mandate yet whimpered that they ruled as orphaned heirs.

sentences.zh: 《司馬法》廣陳三代，曰：古者六尺爲步，步百爲畝，畝百爲夫，夫三爲屋，屋三爲井。

translations.literal: The "Sima Fa" broadly expounds the Three Dynasties, saying: In antiquity six chi made a pace, a hundred paces made a mu, a hundred mu made a husband-unit, three husband-units made a roof-cluster, three roof-clusters made a well-field.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Canons of Sima recount the Three Ages: six feet to the pace, a hundred paces to the survey mu, a hundred mu to a husband's share, three husbands to a cluster, three clusters to the sacred well of nine farms.

sentences.zh: 井方一里，是爲九夫，八家共之。

translations.literal: A well is a square of one li; this constitutes nine husband-slots; eight households share it.
translations.idiomatic: Each well squared a li, carved nine strips, and yoked eight families to its central lord's strip.

sentences.zh: 一夫一婦受私田百畝，公田十畝，是爲八百八十畝，餘二十畝爲廬舍，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相救。

translations.literal: One husband one wife receive private fields a hundred mu, public field ten mu—this makes eight hundred eighty mu; the remaining twenty mu are hut-sites; going out and entering they befriend; watching and guarding they assist; in sickness they rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Each couple drew a hundred private mu and ten for the common furrow—880 mu under tillage and twenty for roofs; neighbors pledged friendship at every gate, stood night watch together, and nursed fevers shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 民受田，上田夫百畝，中田夫二百畝，下田夫三百畝，歲受耕之，爰自其處。

translations.literal: The people receive fields: on upper fields a husband has a hundred mu; on middle fields two hundred mu; on lower fields three hundred mu; yearly they receive and till them, shifting accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers drew graded plots—one hundred mu on rich soil, two hundred on middling, three hundred on lean—rotating with the seasons as the law nudged them along.

sentences.zh: 其家眾男爲餘夫，亦以口受田如此。

translations.literal: The family's multitude of males as surplus husbands likewise by mouth receive fields in this manner.
translations.idiomatic: Extra grown sons counted as surplus tillers and earned more acreage by the same mouth tally.

sentences.zh: 士工商家受田，五口乃當農夫一口。

translations.literal: Scholar, artisan, and merchant households receive fields; five mouths equal one peasant mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry, craftsmen, and merchants held land too, yet five of their mouths paid as one plowman's share.

sentences.zh: 有賦有稅，稅謂公田什一及工商衡虞之入也，賦供車馬甲兵士從之役。

translations.literal: There are fu and shui; shui means the public-field one-tenth and the income of artisans, merchants, weighers, and marsh-keepers; fu supplies chariots, horses, armor, weapons, accompanyers, and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Two ledgers ran: "tax" skimmed the lord's tenth and the townsmen who trafficked scales and marshes; "levy" horseshoed chariots, buckled armor, and dragooned footmen.

sentences.zh: 民年二十受田，六十歸田。

translations.literal: The people at age twenty receive fields; at sixty they return fields.
translations.idiomatic: A man took land at twenty and surrendered it at sixty.

sentences.zh: 種穀必雜五種，以備災旱。

translations.literal: Planting grain must mix five kinds, to prepare for disaster and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Every field blended five grains so famine could not kill the harvest whole.

sentences.zh: 田中不得有樹，以妨五穀。

translations.literal: In fields there must not be trees, lest they obstruct the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Grain land stayed shadeless—no orchard stealing sunlight from the staples.

sentences.zh: 環廬種桑柘，菜茹有畦，瓜瓠果蓏植於疆埸，雞㹠狗豕無失其時。

translations.literal: Around huts plant mulberry and zhe; vegetables have beds; melons, gourds, fruits, and berries plant on boundaries; chickens, pigs, dogs, and swine—do not miss their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberries hugged each roof, kitchen gardens squared their rows, melons straggled along the headlands, and every yard timed its fowl and hogs to the turning moons.

sentences.zh: 閭有序，鄉有庠，序以明教，庠以行禮。

translations.literal: A lü has a village school; a xiang has a hall; the village school clarifies teaching; the hall conducts rites.
translations.idiomatic: Each lane kept a school where royal lessons shone, each district a hall where elders rehearsed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 司馬之法，官設六軍之眾，因井田而制軍。

translations.literal: The Sima method: officials establish the mass of six armies; according to well-fields they regulate armies.
translations.idiomatic: The war statutes called up six hosts, threading regiment on regiment straight from the well-field grid.

sentences.zh: 令地方一里爲井，井十爲通，通十爲成，成方十里。

translations.literal: [They] ordered that land be measured: one li square makes one well-field unit (jing); ten jing make a tong; ten tong make a cheng; one cheng spans ten li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statute, one square li formed a jing, ten jing made a tong, ten tong a cheng, and a cheng stood ten li to the side.

sentences.zh: 成十爲終，終十爲同，同方百里。

translations.literal: Ten cheng make a zhong; ten zhong make a tong; one tong extends one hundred li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: A stack of ten cheng became a zhong; ten zhong a tong, and each tong measured a hundred li on a side.

sentences.zh: 同十爲封，封十爲畿，畿方千里。

translations.literal: Ten tong make a feng; ten feng make a ji; a ji spans one thousand li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Ten tong made a feng; ten feng a royal ringland (ji), a thousand li on every side—the core demesne of the crown.

sentences.zh: 故井四爲邑，邑四爲丘，丘十六井，有戎馬一匹，牛三頭。

translations.literal: Therefore four jing make a settlement (yi); four yi make a mound-district (qiu); a qiu holds sixteen jing, with one war-horse and three oxen.
translations.idiomatic: So four jing grouped into a yi, four yi into a qiu holding sixteen jing, supporting one mount for war and three draft oxen.

sentences.zh: 四丘爲甸，甸六十四井也，有戎馬四匹，兵車一乘，牛十二頭，甲士三人，卒七十二人。

translations.literal: Four qiu make a dian; a dian is sixty-four jing, with four war-horses, one war-chariot, twelve oxen, three armored warriors, and seventy-two foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Four qiu formed a dian of sixty-four jing, fit for four chargers, a single battle chariot, twelve oxen, three armored men, and seventy-two rank-and-file troops.

translations.literal: This is called the rule for holding a chariot.
translations.idiomatic: This defined the military levy for one chariot.

sentences.zh: 一同百里，提封萬井，除山川、坑岸、城池、邑居、園囿、街路三千六百井，定出賦六千四百井，戎馬四百匹，兵車百乘，此卿大夫菜地之大者也，是謂百乘之家。

translations.literal: One tong measures one hundred li square; its tifeng is ten thousand jing; after removing mountains, rivers, pits, banks, walls and moats of cities, towns and residences, parks and enclosures, and thoroughfares—three thousand six hundred jing—the taxable assessment fixes six thousand four hundred jing, four hundred war-horses, and one hundred chariots; this is the greatest among ministers' and grandees' provision fiefs, called a house of one hundred chariots.
translations.idiomatic: For a single tong, a hundred li on a side and ten thousand jing under seal, once mountains, waters, wasteland, fortifications, settlements, hunting parks, and roads had been set aside—three thousand six hundred jing—the remaining sixty-four hundred jing furnished four hundred mounts and a full hundred chariots; that was the largest estate granted to ministers and great officers, the so-called household of a hundred chariots.

sentences.zh: 一封三百六十六里，提封十萬井，定出賦六萬四千井，戎馬四千匹，兵車千乘，此謂諸侯之大者也，謂之千乘之國。

translations.literal: One feng measures three hundred sixty-six li square; its tifeng is one hundred thousand jing; the taxable assessment fixes sixty-four thousand jing, four thousand war-horses, and one thousand chariots; this is called a great feudal lord, termed a state of a thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: A feng of three hundred sixty-six li to the side embraced a hundred thousand jing, with sixty-four thousand taxable jing sustaining four thousand horses and a thousand chariots—the scale of the greatest feudal lords, a true thousand-chariot polity.

sentences.zh: 天子畿內方千里，提封百萬井，定出賦六十四萬井，戎馬四萬匹，兵車萬乘，戎卒七十二萬人，故天子稱萬乘之主焉。

translations.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's ji, a thousand li square, the tifeng is a million jing; the taxable assessment fixes six hundred forty thousand jing, forty thousand war-horses, ten thousand chariots, and seven hundred twenty thousand troops; therefore the Son of Heaven is called lord of ten thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Across the royal thousand-li square, a million jing yielded taxable ground for sixty-four myriad jing, mounting forty thousand horses, ten thousand chariots, and seven hundred twenty thousand soldiers—whence the sovereign earned the title of ruler of ten thousand chariots.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇既得志於天下，訪周之敗，以爲處士橫議，諸侯尋戈，四夷交侵，以弱見奪，於是削去五等焉。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin had realized his ambition in All-under-Heaven, he reviewed Zhou's defeat and took it that recluses bandied reckless opinions, feudal lords raised halberds one upon another, the four outer peoples invaded in turn, and Zhou, through weakness, was stripped away; thereupon he abolished the five noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qin Shihuang had mastered the realm, he read Zhou's fall as the fruit of unbridled private debate among scholars, incessant war among lords, and relentless barbarian pressure that preyed on weakness—and scrapped the entire five-rank aristocracy.

sentences.zh: 漢興，創艾亡秦孤立而敗，於是割裂封疆，立爵二等，功臣侯者百有餘邑。

translations.literal: When Han rose, [rulers] learned from the wound of fallen Qin's isolation and collapse; therefore they carved territory into enfeoffments, set up two grades of nobility, and merit marquises held more than a hundred towns.
translations.idiomatic: Han, still smarting from Qin's rigid centralization and swift ruin, reapportioned the map into fiefs, limited noble rank to two tiers, and let more than a hundred merit marquises each hold a patch of soil.

sentences.zh: 于時民罹秦項，戶口彫弊，大侯不過萬家，小者五六百戶，而尊王子弟，大啟九國。

translations.literal: At that time the people had suffered under Qin and Xiang; households and population were depleted; great marquises did not exceed ten thousand households, small ones five or six hundred households; yet [the court] honored imperial sons and younger brothers and vastly opened up nine kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Households were still shattered by Qin exactions and Chu civil war, so even great marquisates counted fewer than ten thousand families and small ones only five or six hundred—yet the throne lavished titles on imperial kinsmen and planted nine sprawling royal domains.

sentences.zh: 古者有分土而無分民，若乃大者跨州連郡，小則十有餘城，以戶口爲差降，略封疆之遠近，所謂分民自漢始也。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was division of land but no division of people; but in this case the large [fiefs] spanned provinces and linked commanderies, the small had ten-odd cities, and [status] was graded by registered households, neglecting how far the borders lay; what is called dividing the people begins with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings had parceled soil, not registered subjects; now the largest apanages covered whole provinces, the modest still held a dozen walled towns, and rank tracked headcounts while the distances of frontiers hardly mattered—the peculiar Han practice of parting the people among lords had begun.

sentences.zh: 起雁門以東，盡遼陽，爲燕代。

translations.literal: From Yanmen eastward to the farthest reach of Liaoyang—this formed Yan and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The block running east from the Yanmen line through Liaoyang was reckoned as Yan and Dai together.

sentences.zh: 常山以南，太行左轉，渡河濟，漸于海，爲齊趙。

translations.literal: South of Mount Chang, the Taihang turning left, crossing the He and Ji [rivers], reaching to the sea—this formed Qi and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: South of Changshan, with the Taihang swinging east, the Yellow River and Ji ford behind them, and the coast ahead, stretched Qi and Zhao as one bloc.

sentences.zh: 穀泗以注，奄有龜蒙，爲梁楚。

translations.literal: Where the Gu and Si flow in, covering Gui and Meng—this formed Liang and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Gu and Si confluence and the Gui-Meng massif lay the territories reckoned as Liang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 東帶江湖，薄會稽，爲荊吳。

translations.literal: Belted to the east by the Yangtze and lakes, pressing against Kuaiji—this formed Jing and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: A strip belted by the great river and southern lakes, nosing to Kuaiji, counted as Jing and Wu.

sentences.zh: 北界淮瀕，略廬衡，爲淮南。

translations.literal: Bordered on the north by the Huai shore, taking in Lu and Heng—this formed Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: North along the Huai's bank, drawing in the Lu and Heng ranges, stood the block called Huainan.

sentences.zh: 波漢之陽，亙九疑，爲長沙。

translations.literal: Beyond the northern bank of the Han, spanning the Jiuyi—this formed Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Han sweep and through the Jiuyi peaks ran the Changsha alignment.

sentences.zh: 諸侯比境，周匝三垂，外接胡越。

translations.literal: The feudal lords shared adjoining borders; they wrapped the three outer margins; outward they connected to Hu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The vassals stood shoulder to shoulder along the inner rim, girdling three frontiers while opening outward onto the Hu steppe and southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 天子自有三河、東郡、潁川、南陽，自江陵以西至巴蜀，北至雲中，西至隴西，與京師內史，凡十五郡。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven himself held the Three He, Dong commandery, Yingchuan, Nanyang; from Jiangling west to Ba and Shu; north to Yunzhong; west to Longxi; together with the capital Neishi—in all fifteen commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen commanderies—the Three He core plus Dong, Yingchuan, and Nanyang, the western arc from Jiangling through Ba and Shu, the northern bastions Yunzhong, the Longxi line, and the metropolitan Neishi—remained directly in the emperor's hand.

sentences.zh: 文帝采賈生之議分齊趙，景帝用朝錯之計削吳楚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen adopted Jia Yi's proposal to divide Qi and Zhao; Emperor Jing employed Chao Cuo's plan to pare away Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi split Qi and Zhao on Jia Yi's advice; Jingdi pared the great eastern kingdoms with Chao Cuo's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 武帝施主父之冊，下推恩之令，使諸侯王得分戶邑以封子弟，不行黜陟，而藩國自析。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu applied Zhufu Yi's memorial and issued the order to push favor outward, causing kings of the feudal states to divide household-towns to enfeoff sons and younger brothers; without carrying out demotions or promotions, the buffer kingdoms split of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi promulgated Zhufu Yi's memorial as the "push-the-grace" edict, letting every king slice his domain to enfeoff heirs—no formal downgrading needed—and watched the great apanages quietly fracture.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，齊分爲七，趙分爲六，梁分爲五，淮南分爲三。

translations.literal: From this time on, Qi split into seven, Zhao into six, Liang into five, Huainan into three.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Qi splintered seven ways, Zhao six, Liang five, Huainan three.

sentences.zh: 皇子始立者大國不過十餘城，長沙、燕、代雖有舊名，皆亡南北邊矣。

translations.literal: When imperial sons were first established, great states had no more than ten-odd cities; Changsha, Yan, and Dai, though bearing old names, had all lost their northern and southern frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: A freshly minted imperial son might rule barely a dozen counties; mighty old names like Changsha, Yan, and Dai had become hollow titles stripped of their former north and south marches.

sentences.zh: 自文景與民休息，至平帝元始二年，民戶千二百二十三萬三千六十二，口五千九百五十九萬四千九百七十八，其地東西九千三百二里，南北萬三千三百六十八里。

translations.literal: From Wen and Jing, who rested the people, to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year: twelve million two hundred thirty-three thousand sixty-two households; fifty-nine million five hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred seventy-eight persons; the territory nine thousand three hundred two li east-west, thirteen thousand three hundred sixty-eight li north-south.
translations.idiomatic: The restorative reigns of Wen and Jing carried down to Pingdi's Yuanshi 2 (1 CE), when the registers recorded 12,233,062 households and 59,594,978 people across 9,302 li east–west and 13,368 li north–south.

translations.literal: In general, one ting every ten li; a ting has a chief.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly every ten li stood a courier lodge (ting) headed by a chief.

sentences.zh: 十亭一鄉，鄉有三老，有秩嗇夫、游徼各一人。

translations.literal: Ten ting make one xiang; a xiang has three elders, one ranked sefu, and one patrol officer (youjiao), one each.
translations.idiomatic: Ten ting formed a township with three elders plus a single salaried sefu and a roving constable.

sentences.zh: 縣大率方百里，民稠則減，稀則曠，鄉亭亦如之。

translations.literal: Counties were generally one hundred li square; if people were dense it was reduced, if sparse it was expanded; xiang and ting likewise.
translations.idiomatic: A county normally covered a hundred-li square, trimmed where crowded, widened where thin, township and lodge scales following suit.

translations.literal: All were Qin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of these rules descended from Qin.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，不踰前制，東海王彊以去就有禮，故優以大封，兼食魯郡二十九縣，其餘稱爲寵錫者，兼一郡而已。

translations.literal: At Guangwu's restoration [the system] did not exceed prior norms; the Prince of Donghai, Qiang, for his proper bearing in choosing to stay or go, was therefore favored with a great enfeoffment, also drawing sustenance from twenty-nine counties of Lu commandery; the rest who were said to receive doted grants merely added one commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu revived Han he held to the old ceilings—except Liu Qiang, Prince of Donghai, whose scrupulous conduct in yielding the crown earned him a double stipend through twenty-nine Lu counties while other favorites merely tacked on a single commandery.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝永壽三年，戶千六十七萬七千九百六十，口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六，[3]斯亦戶口之滋殖者也。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Huan's Yongshou third year: ten million six hundred seventy-seven thousand nine hundred sixty households; fifty-six million four hundred eighty-six thousand eight hundred fifty-six persons; this too was the increase and multiplication of registered population.
