translations.idiomatic: By Huan's Yongshou 3 (157 CE) the rolls listed 10,677,960 households and 56,486,856 souls—clear evidence that the people were breeding back.

sentences.zh: 獻帝建安元年拜曹操爲鎮東將軍，封費亭侯。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xian's Jian'an first year [the court] appointed Cao Cao General Who Stabilizes the East and enfeoffed him Marquis of the Feiting precinct.
translations.idiomatic: In Xian's first year of Jian'an, Cao Cao received appointment as General Who Stabilizes the East and an enfeoffment as Marquis of the Feiting precinct.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，初制封王之庶子爲鄉公，嗣王之庶子爲亭侯，[4]公侯之庶子爲亭伯。

translations.literal: In Wei Wendi's Huangchu third year, an edict first ruled that the king's sons by secondary wives became xiang dukes, the heir-king's sons by secondary wives became ting marquises, and the sons by secondary wives of dukes and marquises became ting earls.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 3 assigned a king's younger sons by secondary consorts the rank of village duke, an heir-apparent's younger brothers by secondary consorts the rank of precinct marquis, and a duke's or marquis's younger sons by secondary consorts the rank of precinct baron.

sentences.zh: 劉備章武元年，亦以郡國封建諸王，或遙採嘉名，不由檢土地所出。

translations.literal: In Liu Bei's Zhangwu first year, he likewise used commanderies and kingdoms to enfeoff the various kings; some took fine titles from afar, without examining what the lands produced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwu 1 watched Liu Bei enfeoff his kinsmen with commandery-sized kingdoms, sometimes borrowing glamorous Central Plain toponyms that bore little relation to local revenue.

sentences.zh: 其戶二十萬，男女口九十萬。

translations.literal: Its households were two hundred thousand; male and female mouths nine hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That realm counted two hundred thousand households and nine hundred thousand persons all told.

sentences.zh: 孫權赤烏五年，亦取中州嘉號封建諸王。

translations.literal: In Sun Quan's Chiwu fifth year, he likewise took fine designations from the Central Plain to enfeoff the various kings.
translations.idiomatic: In his fifth Chiwu year Sun Quan did the same, granting his kinsmen splendid Central-Plain sobriquets.

sentences.zh: 其戶五十二萬三千，男女口二百四十萬。

translations.literal: Its households were five hundred twenty-three thousand; male and female mouths two million four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His domains mustered 523,000 households and 2,400,000 people.

sentences.zh: 晉文帝爲晉王，命裴秀等建立五等之制，惟安平郡公孚邑萬戶，制度如魏諸王。

translations.literal: When Jin Wendi was King of Jin, he ordered Pei Xiu and others to erect the five-grade system; only the Commandery Duke of Anping, Fu, had a fief of ten thousand households; his institutions matched Wei's kings.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin's king-maker Sima Zhao ordered Pei Xiu to draft the five noble ranks: only Sima Fu, duke of Anping commandery, kept the full ten-thousand-household scale befitting a Wei royal.

sentences.zh: 其餘縣公邑千八百戶，地方七十五里；

translations.literal: The rest of the district dukes (xianguo gong) had fiefs of one thousand eight hundred households; the territory seventy-five li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Other county-level dukes held 1,800 households across seventy-five li to the side.

sentences.zh: 大國侯邑千六百戶，地方七十里；

translations.literal: A great-state marquis had a fief of one thousand six hundred households; the territory seventy li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Senior-grade marquises drew 1,600 households over seventy li.

sentences.zh: 次國侯邑千四百戶，地方六十五里；

translations.literal: A secondary-state marquis had a fief of one thousand four hundred households; the territory sixty-five li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Next-rank marquises held 1,400 households across sixty-five li.

sentences.zh: 大國伯邑千二百戶，地方六十里；

translations.literal: A great-state earl (bo) had a fief of one thousand two hundred households; the territory sixty li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Senior earls received 1,200 households within sixty li.

sentences.zh: 次國伯邑千戶，地方五十五里；

translations.literal: A secondary-state earl had a fief of one thousand households; the territory fifty-five li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Junior earls kept a thousand households spread over fifty-five li.

sentences.zh: 大國子邑八百戶，地方五十里；

translations.literal: A great-state viscount (zi) had a fief of eight hundred households; the territory fifty li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Senior viscounts had eight hundred households inside fifty li.

sentences.zh: 次國子邑六百戶，地方四十五里；

translations.literal: A secondary-state viscount had a fief of six hundred households; the territory forty-five li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser viscounts owned six hundred households across forty-five li.

sentences.zh: 男邑四百戶，地方四十里。

translations.literal: A baron (nan) had a fief of four hundred households; the territory forty li square on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Lowest baronies stopped at four hundred households and forty li.

sentences.zh: [5]武帝泰始元年，封諸王以郡爲國。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taishi first year, he enfeoffed the various kings with commanderies as their kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 1 made each prince's kingdom co-extensive with an entire commandery.

sentences.zh: 邑二萬戶爲大國，置上中下三軍，兵五千人；

translations.literal: Twenty thousand households in the fief is a great state; it establishes upper, middle, and lower armies—five thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: A great kingdom—20,000 registered households—fielded upper, middle, and lower brigades totaling 5,000 men.

sentences.zh: 邑萬戶爲次國，置上軍下軍，兵三千人；

translations.literal: Ten thousand households in the fief is a secondary state; it establishes upper and lower armies—three thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary realms of ten thousand households maintained upper and lower corps with 3,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 五千戶爲小國，置一軍，兵千五百人。

translations.literal: Five thousand households is a small state; it establishes one army—one thousand five hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Petty kingdoms of 5,000 families mustered a single army of 1,500.

translations.literal: The kings did not go to their kingdoms; they held office in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Princes stayed in Luoyang on court salary rather than residing in their nominal realms.

sentences.zh: 罷五等之制，公侯邑萬戶以上爲大國，五千戶以上爲次國，不滿五千戶爲小國。

translations.literal: The five-grade system was abolished; dukes and marquises with fiefs of ten thousand households or more were great states, five thousand or more secondary states, fewer than five thousand small states.
translations.idiomatic: After the five-rank scheme lapsed, ducal or marquisal estates of ten thousand households or more counted as great polities, those from five thousand upward as secondary, and those below five thousand as small.

sentences.zh: 太康元年，平吳，大凡戶二百四十五萬九千八百四十，口一千六百一十六萬三千八百六十三。

translations.literal: In Taikang first year, when Wu was pacified, in the main there were two million four hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred forty households; sixteen million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-three persons.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 1, the year Wu fell, the empire tallied roughly 2,459,840 households and 16,163,863 mouths.

sentences.zh: 而江左諸國並三分食一，元帝渡江，太興元年，始制九分食一。

translations.literal: But the various kingdoms east of the Yangtze all took one-third [of their commanderies' revenue]; after Yuan Emperor crossed the Yangtze, in Taixing first year, they first instituted taking one-ninth.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river every apanage skimmed a third of its host commandery until Yuan crossed; Taixing 1 trimmed the royal share to one-ninth.

translations.literal: This follows the land of Yu's Tribute's Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter tracks the Yu Province demarcated in the "Tribute of Yu."

sentences.zh: 及漢武帝，初置司隸校尉，所部三輔、三河諸郡。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, he first established the Colonel Director of Retainers; what it commanded were the three adjuncts, Three Rivers, and the various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi created the Colonel Director of Retainers to oversee the three metropolitan adjuncts and the Three Rivers commanderies.

sentences.zh: 其界西得雍州之京兆、馮翊、扶風三郡，北得冀州之河東、河內二郡，東得豫州之弘農、河南二郡，郡凡七。

translations.literal: Its bounds: west it took three commanderies from Yongzhou—Jingzhao, Fengyi, Fufeng; north it took two from Jizhou—Hedong, Henei; east it took two from Yuzhou—Hongnong, Henan—in all seven commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel's seven commanderies drew Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng from Yongzhou, Hedong and Henei from Jizhou, and Hongnong and Henan from Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 位望隆于牧伯，[6]銀印青綬。

translations.literal: Dignity and repute surpassed those of shepherds and chiefs; silver seal and green ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel outranked provincial shepherds, badge by silver seal and green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 及光武都洛陽，司隸所部與前漢不異。

translations.literal: When Guangwu made his capital at Luoyang, what the Colonel Director of Retainers commanded did not differ from Western Han.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's move to Luoyang left the colonel's remit matching Western Han's footprint.

sentences.zh: 魏氏受禪，即都漢宮，司隸所部河南、河東、河內、弘農并冀州之平陽，合五郡，置司州。

translations.literal: When Wei received the abdication, it immediately took the Han palace as capital; what the Colonel commanded—Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, together with Pingyang from Jizhou—five commanderies combined—was set up as Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei inherited Luoyang's palaces, folded Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, and Pingyang commandery from Jizhou into a five-commandery Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 晉仍居魏都，乃以三輔還屬雍州，分河南立滎陽，分雍州之京兆立上洛，廢東郡立頓丘，遂定名司州，以司隸校尉統之。

translations.literal: Jin still dwelled in Wei's capital; therefore it returned the three adjuncts to Yongzhou, split Henan to establish Xingyang, split Jingzhao from Yongzhou to establish Shangluo, abolished Dong commandery and established Dunqiu—thereupon the name Sizhou was fixed, governed by the Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin stayed put but reassigned the three Qin adjuncts back to Yong, carved Xingyang out of Henan, Shangluo out of Jingzhao, traded Dong commandery for Dunqiu, and locked the new layout under the colonel's eye.

sentences.zh: 州統郡一十二，縣一百，戶四十七萬五千七百。

translations.literal: The zhou governed twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, and four hundred seventy-five thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: This Sizhou ruled twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, and 475,700 households.

translations.literal: The transmitted text marks a seventh scholium.
translations.idiomatic: Here the edition inserts a marginal gloss in the commentary tradition.

translations.literal: Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Henan commandery.

translations.literal: The Han court created this commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founding administration chartered Henan commandery here.

sentences.zh: 統縣十二，戶一十一萬四千四百。

translations.literal: It governed twelve counties and had one hundred fourteen thousand four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw twelve counties and 114,400 registered households.

translations.literal: A metropolitan prefect (yin) headed the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The senior magistrate bore the metropolitan yin title.

translations.literal: Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang.

translations.literal: The county seat stationed a captain (wei).
translations.idiomatic: A county captain kept order in the county seat.

translations.idiomatic: By the last years of Emperor Hui, not a handbreadth of Yan Province remained free: the whole region had fallen under Shi Le’s heel.

sentences.zh: 後石季龍改陳留郡爲建昌郡，屬洛州。

translations.literal: Later Shi Jilong changed Chenliu Commandery to Jianchang Commandery, belonging to Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Shi Hu—Jilong by his intimate name—renamed Chenliu as Jianchang and folded it into Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 是時遺黎南渡，元帝僑置兗州，寄居京口。

translations.literal: At that time surviving people crossed south; Emperor Yuan established Yan Province in exile and lodged it at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors poured south across the river; Emperor Yuan therefore “borrowed” a patch of land for a shadow Yan Province, its nominal seat at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 明帝以郗鑒爲刺史，寄居廣陵，置濮陽、濟陰、高平、太山等郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made Xi Jian regional inspector, lodged at Guangling, and set up Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming named Xi Jian inspector and moved the office to Guangling, carving out nominal jurisdictions—Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and more—on paper if not always on soil.

sentences.zh: 後改爲南兗州，或還江南，或居盱眙，或居山陽。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to Southern Yan Province, sometimes returning south of the Yangtze, sometimes dwelling at Xuyi, sometimes at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Renamed Southern Yan, it drifted: now back below the Yangtze, now perched at Xuyi, now at Shanyang—always provisional, like memory of a lost map.

sentences.zh: 後始割地爲境，常居廣陵，南與京口對岸。

translations.literal: Later they began to carve land as borders, usually residing at Guangling, south facing Jingkou across the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did real territory attach to the name; the inspectorate settled habitually at Guangling, its southern bank staring across the water at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，於北譙界立陳留郡。

translations.literal: Xiankang fourth year, on the border of Northern Qiao they established Chenliu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiankang they drew a Chenliu Commandery on the frontier of Northern Qiao—another line on the map where refugees might pretend the old heartland still existed.

sentences.zh: 安帝分廣陵郡之建陵、臨江、如皋、寧海、蒲濤五縣置山陽郡，屬南兗州。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai split from Guangling Commandery five counties—Jianling, Linjiang, Rugao, Ninghai, and Putao—and established Shanyang Commandery, belonging to Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai peeled off Jianling, Linjiang, Rugao, Ninghai, and Putao from Guangling to form a new Shanyang Commandery under Southern Yan—a fresh grid for an old grief.

translations.literal: According to the Tribute of Yu it was the land between Jing and the River.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute of Yu draws it as the country between the Jing hills and the great river.

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: “South of the river is called Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou declares: ‘South of the river lies Yu Province.’

sentences.zh: 」豫者舒也，言稟中和之氣，性理安舒也。

translations.literal: ” “Yu” means ease; it says they receive balanced harmonizing qi, nature and pattern calm and ease.
translations.idiomatic: ‘Yu’ speaks of ease—of a region imbued with balanced breath, whose people grow temperate and unhurried.

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「鉤鈐星別爲豫州。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuan Ming Bao says: “The hook-and-hasp stars separately constitute Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphon Spring and Autumn Yuan Ming Bao adds: ‘The hook-and-clasp stars mark out Yu Province among the fields of heaven.’

sentences.zh: 」地界，西自華山，東至于淮，北自濟，南界荊山。

translations.literal: ” The territorial bounds: west from Mount Hua, east reaching to the Huai, north from the Ji, south bounded by Mount Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On earth its borders ran from Mount Hua in the west to the Huai in the east, from the Ji River northward to Mount Jing in the south.

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，以爲三川、河東、南陽、潁川、碭、泗水、薛七郡。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm, making seven commanderies: Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin swallowed the world, it sorted this ground into seven commanderies—Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue.

sentences.zh: 漢改三川爲河南郡，武帝置十三州，豫州舊名不改，以河南、河東二郡屬司隸，又以南陽屬荊州。

translations.literal: Han changed Sanchuan to Henan Commandery; Emperor Wu established thirteen provinces; Yu Province’s old name was unchanged, but Henan and Hedong two commanderies belonged to the metropolitan inspectorate, and also they attached Nanyang to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Han rechristened Sanchuan as Henan; Emperor Wu’s thirteen circuits left the name Yu undisturbed even as Henan and Hedong passed to the capital intendancy and Nanyang was folded into Jing.

sentences.zh: 先是，改泗水曰沛郡，改碭郡曰梁，改薛曰魯，分梁沛立汝南郡，分潁川立淮陽郡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sishui was changed to Pei Commandery, Dang Commandery was changed to Liang, Xue was changed to Lu; Liang and Pei were split to establish Runan Commandery, and Yingchuan was split to establish Huaiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Already Sishui had become Pei, Dang had become Liang, Xue had turned into Lu; Runan was cut from Liang and Pei, Huaiyang from Yingchuan—the geometry of empire endlessly redrawn.

sentences.zh: 後漢章帝改淮陽曰陳郡。

translations.literal: Later Han’s Emperor Zhang changed Huaiyang to Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han’s Emperor Zhang traded the name Huaiyang for Chen.

sentences.zh: 魏武分沛立譙郡，魏文分汝南立弋陽郡。

translations.literal: Wei Wu split Pei to establish Qiao Commandery; Wei Wen split Runan to establish Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao—posthumously Wei Wu—split Pei to birth Qiao; his son Cao Pi, Wei Wen, split Runan to raise Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受命，又分潁川立襄城郡，分汝南立汝陰郡，合陳郡于梁國。

translations.literal: And when Emperor Wu received the mandate, again he split Yingchuan to establish Xiangcheng Commandery, split Runan to establish Ruyin Commandery, and merged Chen Commandery into the Principality of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, he split Yingchuan again for Xiangcheng, Runan for Ruyin, and wove old Chen into the princedom of Liang.

translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Mu’s fifth Yonghe year Murong Jun crowned himself at Ji, and chroniclers speak of Former Yan.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Murong Jun moved the capital to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Murong Jun carried his court south to Ye.

translations.literal: Murong Jun died, and his son Murong Wei was extinguished by Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun’s death left his heir Murong Wei to face Fu Jian, who erased their throne.

sentences.zh: 堅敗，地復入慕容垂，是爲後燕。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was defeated, and the lands again entered Murong Chui; this was Later Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian fell, Murong Chui gathered the fragments and styled his realm Later Yan.

translations.literal: Murong Chui died, and Murong Bao moved to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui’s son Murong Bao, seeing the roof collapse, withdrew toward Helong.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢冀州之域，於周爲幽州界，漢屬右北平郡。

translations.literal: According to the Tribute of Yu it lies in Jizhou’s territory; under Zhou it was the border of Youzhou; under Han it belonged to Youbeiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute of Yu classifies this ground with Jizhou; the Zhou saw it as Youzhou’s marches; Han filed it under Youbeiping.

sentences.zh: 後漢末，公孫度自號平州牧。

translations.literal: Near the end of Later Han, Gongsun Du styled himself shepherd of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Later Han, Gongsun Du invented the title “shepherd of Pingzhou” and answered to no one.

sentences.zh: 及其子康、康子文懿並擅據遼東，東夷九種皆服事焉。

translations.literal: Together with his son Gongsun Kang and Kang’s son Gongsun Yuan (posthumous title Wenyi), they seized and held Liaodong; the nine eastern Yi kinds all served them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du, then Gongsun Kang, then Gongsun Yuan—who would receive the posthumous title Wenyi—for three generations clamped Liaodong shut, and nine eastern peoples paid them court.

sentences.zh: 魏置東夷校尉，居襄平，而分遼東、昌黎、玄菟、帶方、樂浪五郡爲平州，後還合爲幽州。

translations.literal: Wei set up the Commandant of the Eastern Yi based at Xiangping, split the five commanderies Liaodong, Changli, Xuantu, Daifang, and Lelang into Ping Province, and later merged them back into You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, a Commandant of the Eastern Yi sat at Xiangping while five frontier commanderies—Liaodong, Changli, Xuantu, Daifang, and Lelang—were carved out as Ping Province, though the whole arrangement was later folded back into You Province.

sentences.zh: 及文懿滅後，有護東夷校尉，居襄平。

translations.literal: After Wenyi was destroyed, there was a Protecting Commandant of the Eastern Yi, based at Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Yuan fell, the court replaced the old post with a Protecting Commandant of the Eastern Yi, again headquartered at Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年十月，分昌黎、遼東、玄菟、帶方、樂浪等郡國五置平州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second Xianning year, it split off Changli, Liaodong, Xuantu, Daifang, Lelang, and so on—five commanderies and principalities—to establish Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Xianning, the throne peeled away five coastal jurisdictions—Changli, Liaodong, Xuantu, Daifang, and Lelang among them—to form the new province of Ping.

sentences.zh: 統縣二十六，戶一萬八千一百。

translations.literal: It governed twenty-six counties and had eighteen thousand one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Its rolls listed twenty-six counties and eighteen thousand one hundred households.

translations.literal: Twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Marginal note twenty-six.

translations.literal: Changli Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Changli Commandery.

translations.literal: Under Han it belonged to the Colonel of the Dependent States in Liaodong; Wei established it as a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the territory answered to the colonial officer for Liaodong's dependent states; Wei elevated it to a full commandery.

translations.literal: It governed two counties; registered households: nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: It held only two counties on the books—nine hundred households in all.

translations.literal: Changli; Bintu.
translations.idiomatic: The seats were Changli and Bintu.

translations.literal: Liaodong Principality.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong Principality.

translations.literal: Qin established it as a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qin first organized the region as a commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢光武以遼東等屬青州後，還幽州。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han attached Liaodong and the rest to Qing Province, then later returned them to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu briefly folded Liaodong into Qing Province before restoring it to You Province.

translations.literal: It governed eight counties; registered households: five thousand four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Eight counties fell under its administration, with some fifty-four hundred households registered.

translations.literal: Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangping.

translations.literal: Where the Commandant of the Eastern Yi resided.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Eastern Yi kept his headquarters here.

sentences.zh: 汶 居就 樂就 安市 西安平 新昌 力城

translations.literal: Wen; Jiujiu; Lejiu; Anshi; Xi'anping; Xinchang; Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Other counties included Wen, Jiujiu, Lejiu, Anshi, Xi'anping, Xinchang, and Licheng.

translations.literal: Lelang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lelang Commandery.

translations.literal: Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founders instituted this commandery.

translations.literal: It governed six counties; registered households: three thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Six counties and thirty-seven hundred households were tallied within its borders.

translations.literal: Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxian—Korea of the classical geographers.

translations.literal: Land enfeoffed to Jizi in Zhou times.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition remembers it as the fief the Zhou kings granted to Jizi.

sentences.zh: 屯有 渾彌 遂城

translations.literal: Tunyou; Hunmi; Suicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tunyou, Hunmi, and Suicheng completed the interior circuit.

translations.literal: The place where Qin began building the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Here, says the note, the First Emperor's wall line began its eastward march.

translations.literal: Loufang; Siwang.
translations.idiomatic: Loufang and Siwang were the remaining seats.

translations.literal: Xuantu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantu Commandery.

translations.literal: Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han state chartered it.

translations.literal: It governed three counties; registered households: three thousand two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Three counties mustered thirty-two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高句麗 望平 高顯

translations.literal: Gaogouli; Wangping; Gaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief towns were Gaogouli, Wangping, and Gaoxian.

translations.literal: Daifang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Daifang Commandery.

translations.literal: Gongsun Du established it.
translations.idiomatic: The warlord Gongsun Du carved it out.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties; registered households: four thousand nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Seven counties reported just under five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 帶方 列口 南新 長岑 提奚 含資 海冥

translations.literal: Daifang; Liekou; Nanxin; Changcen; Tixi; Hanzi; Haiming.
translations.idiomatic: The seats ran Daifang, Liekou, Nanxin, Changcen, Tixi, Hanzi, and Haiming.

sentences.zh: 平州初置，以慕容廆爲刺史，遂屬永嘉之亂，廆爲眾所推。

translations.literal: When Ping Province was first established, Murong Hui was made Inspector; then came the Yongjia disorders, and Hui was pushed forward by the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Province began its brief life with Murong Hui as inspector, but the Yongjia upheavals soon swept the northeast, and local leaders thrust him to the fore.

translations.literal: His grandson Jun moved the capital to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Murong Jun later shifted the court north to Ji.

sentences.zh: 其後慕容垂子寶又遷于和龍，自幽州至於廬溥鎮以南地入於魏。

translations.literal: Later Murong Chui's son Bao moved again to Helong; from You Province down to the land south of Lupu Garrison fell into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui's heir Murong Bao dragged the capital onward to Helong, while everything from You Province south through the Lupu garrison belt slid piecemeal into Northern Wei hands.

sentences.zh: 慕容熙以幽州刺史鎮令支，青州刺史鎮新城，并州刺史鎮凡城，營州刺史鎮宿軍，冀州刺史鎮肥如。

translations.literal: Murong Xi used the Governor of You Province to garrison Lingzhi, the Governor of Qing Province to garrison Xincheng, the Governor of Bing Province to garrison Fancheng, the Governor of Ying Province to garrison Sujun, and the Governor of Ji Province to garrison Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xi parked his You governor at Lingzhi, his Qing governor at Xincheng, his Bing governor at Fancheng, his Ying governor at Sujun, and his Ji governor at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 高雲以幽、冀二州牧鎮肥如，并州刺史鎮白狼。

translations.literal: Gao Yun, as Governor of You and Ji provinces, garrisoned Feiru; the Governor of Bing Province garrisoned Bailang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun coordinated You and Ji from Feiru while his Bing governor held the line at Bailang.

sentences.zh: 後爲馮跋所篡，跋僭號於和龍，是爲後燕，卒滅於魏。

translations.literal: Later he was usurped by Feng Ba; Ba falsely assumed the title at Helong—this was Later Yan—and finally was destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba eventually seized the throne, proclaimed himself at Helong, and styled his state Later Yan until Wei snuffed it out for good.

translations.literal: Taiyuan Principality.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan Principality.

translations.literal: Qin established it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin first chartered it.

translations.literal: It governed thirteen counties; registered households: fourteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen counties and fourteen thousand households lay within its map.

translations.literal: Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang served as the metropolis.

translations.literal: Marquisate prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Its magistrate held the title of marquisate prefect.

sentences.zh: 陽曲 榆次 于離 盂 狼孟 陽邑 大陵 祁 平陶 京陵 中都 鄔

translations.literal: Yangqu; Yuci; Yuli; Yu; Langmeng; Yangyi; Daling; Qi; Pingtao; Jingling; Zhongdu; Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The hinterland included Yangqu, Yuci, Yuli, Yu, Langmeng, Yangyi, Daling, Qi, Pingtao, Jingling, Zhongdu, and Wu.

translations.literal: Shangdang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang Commandery.

translations.literal: Qin established it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's administrators drew its first boundaries.

translations.literal: It governed ten counties; registered households: thirteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ten counties held thirteen thousand households on the cadastre.

sentences.zh: 潞 屯留 壺關 長子 泫氏 高都 銅鞮 湼 襄垣 武鄉

translations.literal: Lu; Tunliu; Huguan; Zhangzi; Xuanshi; Gaodu; Tongti; Nie; Xiangyuan; Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Its seats were Lu, Tunliu, Huguan, Zhangzi, Xuanshi, Gaodu, Tongti, Nie, Xiangyuan, and Wuxiang.

translations.literal: Xihe Principality.
translations.idiomatic: Xihe Principality.

translations.literal: Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: Han mapped it into the empire.

translations.literal: It governed four counties; registered households: six thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Four counties counted sixty-three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 離石 隰城 中陽 介休

translations.literal: Lishi; Xicheng; Zhongyang; Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi, Xicheng, Zhongyang, and Jiexiu rounded out the list.

translations.literal: Leping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Leping Commandery.

translations.literal: Established in the Taishi period.
translations.idiomatic: Jin founded it midway through the Taishi era.

translations.literal: It governed five counties; registered households: four thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Five counties mustered forty-three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 沾 上艾 壽陽 轑陽 樂平

translations.literal: Zhan; Shang'ai; Shouyang; Liaoyang; Leping.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery comprised Zhan, Shang'ai, Shouyang, Liaoyang, and Leping.

translations.literal: Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmen Commandery.

translations.literal: Qin established it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin locked the mountain passes into an administrative unit.

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戶一萬二千七百。〉

translations.literal: It governed eight counties; registered households: twelve thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Eight counties held twelve thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 廣武 崞 𣳫陶 平城 葰人 繁畤 原平 馬邑

translations.literal: Guangwu; Guo; Jutao; Pingcheng; Junren; Fanqi; Yuanping; Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Its seats were Guangwu, Guo, Jutao, Pingcheng, Junren, Fanqi, Yuanping, and Mayi.

translations.literal: Xinxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xinxing Commandery.

translations.literal: Wei established it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao-Wei demarcated it.

translations.literal: It governed five counties; registered households: nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Five counties reported nine thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九原 定襄 雲中 廣牧 晉昌

translations.literal: Jiuyuan; Dingxiang; Yunzhong; Guangmu; Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyuan, Dingxiang, Yunzhong, Guangmu, and Jinchang formed its ring of garrison towns.

translations.literal: Jingzhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Commandery, the capital district.

translations.literal: Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han organized it around metropolitan Chang'an.

translations.literal: It governed nine counties; registered households: forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nine counties housed forty thousand households—dense by frontier standards.

sentences.zh: 長安 杜陵 霸城 藍田 高陸 萬年

translations.literal: Chang'an; Duling; Bacheng; Lantian; Gaolu; Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an, Duling, Bacheng, Lantian, Gaolu, and Wannian anchored the core.

translations.literal: Former Lueyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian occupies the old site of Lueyi.

translations.literal: Xinfeng; Yinban; Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xinfeng, Yinban, and Zheng completed the register.

translations.literal: The town of Duke Huan of Zheng, younger brother of King Xuan of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gazetteers tie Zheng to the Zhou cadet who became Duke Huan of Zheng.

translations.literal: Fengyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi Commandery.

translations.literal: Han established it, named Left Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Han clerks first filed it under the awkward label Left Fengyi.

translations.literal: It governed eight counties; registered households: seven thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Eight counties and seventy-seven hundred households still clung to the Wei River plain.

translations.literal: Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Linjin headed the list.

translations.literal: Formerly Dali; Qin captured it and changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: The old Dali stronghold, renamed once Qin seized it.

sentences.zh: 有河水祠，祠臨晉水，故名。〉

translations.literal: It has a River God shrine; the shrine faces the Linjin River, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: A River God temple fronts the Linjin River—cartographers say that is how the county got its name.

translations.literal: Xiagui.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes Xiagui.

sentences.zh: 〈秦武公伐邽戎，置有上邽，故加「下」。〉

translations.literal: Duke Wu of Qin campaigned against the Gui Rong and, because Shanggui already existed, added "Lower."
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wu of Qin crushed the Gui tribes and marked a new town: because Shanggui already stood upstream, scribes called this one "Lower Gui."

translations.literal: Zhongquan; Pinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongquan and Pinyang followed.

translations.literal: Established by Duke Li of Qin, on the northern bank of the Pin River.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Li founded Pinyang on the sunny north shore of the Pin.

sentences.zh: 粟邑 蓮芍 郃陽 夏陽

translations.literal: Suyi; Lianshao; Heyang; Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: Suyi, Lianshao, Heyang, and Xiayang filled out the eastern rim.

translations.literal: Formerly Shaoliang; King Huiwen of Qin changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: Once called Shaoliang until King Huiwen of Qin rechristened it.

translations.literal: Mount Liang is in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Liang looms to the northwest.

translations.literal: Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈漢武帝以爲主爵都尉，太初中更名右扶風。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han made it a chief commandant for noble ranks; in the Taichu period it was renamed Right Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi first filed it under the chief of noble enfeoffments, then rechristened it Right Fufeng during Taichu.

translations.literal: It governed six counties; registered households: twenty-three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Six counties still supported twenty-three thousand households.

translations.literal: Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyang opens the western cluster.

translations.literal: Established by Emperor Hui of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui chartered the county.

translations.literal: It has Mount Jiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The jagged spine of Mount Jiezhi rises inside its border.

translations.literal: Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Mei lies farther west.

translations.literal: The head of the Chengguo Canal takes in the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengguo Canal lifts its headgates straight from the Wei.

translations.literal: Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong—once the Zhou ritual center—remains a named county.

translations.literal: Marquisate prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief officer ranked as marquisate prefect.

sentences.zh: 有五畤、太昊、黃帝以下祠三百三所。〉

translations.literal: It has the Five Zhi, Taihao, the Yellow Emperor, and below them three hundred three shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Within Yong's precincts crowd the Five Zhi altars, the cults of Taihao and the Yellow Emperor, and more than three hundred lesser shrines besides.

translations.literal: Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Qian takes its name from the river it straddles.

translations.literal: Mount Wu is to the west; ancient texts consider it Mount Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Classic geographers identify Mount Wu to the west with the old name Mount Qian.

translations.literal: Chencang; Meiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chencang and Meiyang border the Qi foothills.

translations.literal: Mount Qi is in the northwest; it was the city King Tai of Zhou made his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Qi guards the northwest—the hill King Tai of Zhou fortified when the Zhou lineage was still young.

translations.literal: Anding Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Anding Commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: This unit dated from Han administration.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties; households numbered five thousand five hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw seven counties and recorded five thousand five hundred households.〉

sentences.zh: 臨涇 朝那 烏氏 都盧 鶉觚 陰密

translations.literal: Lingjing, Chaona, Wushi, Dulou, Chungu, Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: Its seats were Lingjing, Chaona, Wushi, Dulou, Chungu, and Yinmi.

translations.literal: 〈In the Yin age it was the state of Mi.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Tradition identifies it as the Mi polity of Shang times.〉

translations.literal: West Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: The western Chuan tract.

translations.literal: Beidi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Beidi commandery.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Instituted under the Qin.〉

translations.literal: It governed two counties; households two thousand six hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: It held two counties and mustered two thousand six hundred households.〉

translations.literal: Niyang, Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Niyang and Fuping counties.

translations.literal: Shiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiping commandery seat.

translations.literal: 〈Established in the second year of Taishi.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Created in the second year of the Taishi era.

translations.literal: It governed five counties; households eighteen thousand.〉
translations.idiomatic: It administered five counties and eighteen thousand households.〉

translations.literal: Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: The county of Huaili.

translations.literal: 〈Under Qin it was called Feiqiu; Han Gaodi changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Qin atlas listed it as Feiqiu until Gaozu of Han rechristened the place.

translations.literal: There is the Huangshan Palace.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Huangshan Palace stood there.〉

translations.literal: Shiping, Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Shiping together with Wugong.

translations.literal: 〈Mount Taiyi lies east; ancient script took it to be Zhongnan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Taiyi Peak rises to the east; old texts equated it with the Zhongnan range.〉

translations.literal: Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu County.

translations.literal: 〈An ancient state; Qi of Xia campaigned against it.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈A forgotten kingdom said to have been overrun by Qi of Xia.〉

translations.literal: Kuaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison town of Kuaicheng.

translations.literal: Xinping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xinping commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈A Han-era foundation.〉

translations.literal: It governed two counties; households two thousand seven hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Two counties fell under it, with two thousand seven hundred households on the rolls.〉

translations.literal: Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi County.

translations.literal: 〈The Qi River is west.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Qi River ran along its western margin.〉

translations.literal: Fenyi.
translations.idiomatic: The settlement of Fenyi.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，改扶風國爲秦國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui took the throne, Fufeng Principality was changed into Qin Principality.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Hui’s accession the court redesignated the Fufeng fief as the state of Qin.

translations.literal: The capital was moved.
translations.idiomatic: They shifted the seat of government.

translations.literal: After Jianxing, Yongzhou was lost to Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jianxing era ended, Yongzhou slipped from Jin hands into Liu Cong’s Zhao realm.

sentences.zh: 及劉曜徙都長安，改號曰趙，以秦、涼二州牧鎮上邽，朔州牧鎮高平，幽州刺史鎮北地，并州牧鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao moved the capital to Chang’an and changed the title to Zhao, the two shepherds of Qin and Liang garrisoned Shanggui, the shepherd of Shuozhou garrisoned Gaoping, the governor of Youzhou garrisoned Beidi, the shepherd of Bingzhou garrisoned Puban.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao relocated his court to Chang’an and proclaimed the Zhao regime, he posted the joint stewards of Qin and Liang at Shanggui, the Shuozhou steward at Gaoping, the Youzhou governor at Beidi, and the Bingzhou steward at Puban.

translations.literal: Shi Le took Chang’an and again established Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le’s victory at Chang’an brought Yongzhou back onto the map.

sentences.zh: 石氏既敗，苻健僭據關中，又都長安，是爲前秦。

translations.literal: When the Shi clan had been defeated, Fu Jian without warrant seized Guanzhong, again used Chang’an as capital; this was Former Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi house collapsed; Fu Jian then claimed Guanzhong, moved his capital once more to Chang’an, and so began Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 於是乃於雍州置司隸校尉，以豫州刺史鎮許昌，秦州刺史鎮上邽，荊州刺史鎮豐陽，洛州刺史鎮宜陽，并州刺史鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Thereupon in Yongzhou he placed the colonel-director of retainers; the governor of Yuzhou garrisoned Xuchang, the governor of Qinzhou garrisoned Shanggui, the governor of Jingzhou garrisoned Fengyang, the governor of Luozhou garrisoned Yiyang, the governor of Bingzhou garrisoned Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Within Yongzhou he installed a metropolitan intendant; he anchored Yuzhou at Xuchang, Qinzhou at Shanggui, Jingzhou at Fengyang, Luozhou at Yiyang, and Bingzhou at Puban.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時，分司隸爲雍州，分京兆爲咸陽郡，洛州刺史鎮陝城。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian, Sili was split to form Yongzhou; Jingzhao was split to form Xianyang Commandery; the governor of Luozhou garrisoned Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian cleaved the metropolitan circuit into a separate Yongzhou, carved Xianyang commandery out of Jingzhao, and redeployed the Luozhou governor to the Shancheng salient.

sentences.zh: 滅燕之後，分幽州置平州，鎮龍城，幽州刺史鎮薊城，河州刺史鎮枹罕，并州刺史鎮晉陽，豫州刺史鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，雍州刺史鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: After Yan was destroyed, Youzhou was split to create Pingzhou, garrisoning Longcheng; the governor of Youzhou garrisoned Ji City; the governor of Hezhou garrisoned Fuhan; the governor of Bingzhou garrisoned Jinyang; the governor of Yuzhou garrisoned Luoyang; the governor of Yanzhou garrisoned Cangyuan; the governor of Yongzhou garrisoned Puban.
translations.idiomatic: His conquest of Yan prompted a new Pingzhou carved from Youzhou with Longcheng as its hinge; Youzhou itself held Ji, Hezhou watched Fuhan, Bingzhou guarded Jinyang, Yuzhou sat on Luoyang, Yanzhou locked Cangyuan, and Yongzhou returned to Puban.

sentences.zh: 於是移洛州居豐陽，以許昌置東豫州，以荊州刺史鎮襄陽，徐州刺史鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luozhou was moved to dwell at Fengyang; Xuchang was used to set up Eastern Yuzhou; the governor of Jingzhou garrisoned Xiangyang; the governor of Xuzhou garrisoned Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou slid south to Fengyang, Xuchang hosted a shadow Eastern Yuzhou, Jingzhou’s governor pulled back to Xiangyang, and Xuzhou’s to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 既而姚萇滅苻氏，是爲後秦。

translations.literal: Before long Yao Chang destroyed the Fu clan; this was Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yao Chang swept away the Fu house and styled his realm Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 及萇子興克洛陽，以并、冀二州牧鎮蒲阪，豫州牧鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，分司隸領北五郡，置雍州刺史鎮安定。

translations.literal: When Chang’s son Xing took Luoyang, the two shepherds of Bing and Ji garrisoned Puban, the shepherd of Yuzhou garrisoned Luoyang, the governor of Yanzhou garrisoned Cangyuan; Sili was split to lead the northern five commanderies, and a governor of Yongzhou was placed garrisoning Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing’s capture of Luoyang fixed the joint Bing-Ji command at Puban, Yuzhou’s steward at Luoyang, Yanzhou at Cangyuan, while a truncated Sili oversaw five northern counties and a Yongzhou governor held Anding.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓爲劉裕所滅，其地尋入赫連勃勃。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed by Liu Yu, that territory soon entered Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu’s annihilation of Yao Hong left the plateau open; Helian Bobo wasted little time absorbing it.

sentences.zh: 勃勃僭號於統萬，是爲夏。

translations.literal: Bobo without warrant took a regnal title at Tongwan; this was Xia.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongwan, Helian Bobo declared himself emperor of the Xia dynasty that history remembers as Helian Xia.

sentences.zh: 置幽州牧於大城，又平劉義真於長安，遣子璝鎮焉，號曰南臺。

translations.literal: He placed the shepherd of Youzhou at Dacheng; he also pacified Liu Yizhen at Chang’an, sent son Gui to garrison there, calling it the Southern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed a Youzhou steward at Dacheng, crushed Liu Yizhen’s remnant in Chang’an, and left his son Gui there as viceregent under the epithet Southern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 以朔州牧鎮三城，秦州刺史鎮杏城，雍州刺史鎮陰密，并州刺史鎮蒲阪，梁州牧鎮安定，北秦州刺史鎮武功，豫州牧鎮李閏，[30]荊州刺史鎮陝，其州郡之名並不可知也。

translations.literal: The shepherd of Shuozhou garrisoned Sancheng; the governor of Qinzhou garrisoned Xingcheng; the governor of Yongzhou garrisoned Yinmi; the governor of Bingzhou garrisoned Puban; the shepherd of Liangzhou garrisoned Anding; the governor of Northern Qinzhou garrisoned Wugong; the shepherd of Yuzhou garrisoned Li Run; the governor of Jingzhou garrisoned Shan; the names of those provinces and commanderies together are unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: Shuozhou anchored Sancheng, Qinzhou Xingcheng, Yongzhou Yinmi, Bingzhou Puban, Liangzhou Anding, northern Qinzhou Wugong, Yuzhou the Li Run basin, Jingzhou the Shan ford—yet scribal memory of those ephemeral divisions barely survived.

sentences.zh: 然自元帝渡江，所置州亦皆遙領。

translations.literal: Yet from when Emperor Yuan crossed the river, the provinces that were established were also all held in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: Still, once Emperor Yuan ferried the court south, every new province Jin proclaimed existed only as a title held from afar.

sentences.zh: 初以魏該爲雍州刺史，鎮酇城，尋省，僑立始平郡，寄居武當城。

translations.literal: At first Wei Gai was made governor of Yongzhou, garrisoning Zancheng; soon it was abolished; a migrant Shiping Commandery was set up, lodging in Wudang City.
translations.idiomatic: The court first named Wei Gai Yongzhou governor with headquarters at Zancheng, withdrew the post almost at once, then floated a paper Shiping commandery housed inside Wudang’s walls.

sentences.zh: 有秦國流人至江南，改堂邑爲秦郡，僑立尉氏縣屬焉。

translations.literal: There were refugees from Qin Principality who reached Jiangnan; Tangyi was changed into Qin Commandery; a migrant Weishi County was established subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin exiles who washed up along the lower Yangtze persuaded officials to rechristen Tangyi as Qin commandery and hang a nominal Weishi county beneath it.

sentences.zh: 康帝時，庾翼爲荊州刺史，遷鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Kang, Yu Yi was governor of Jingzhou and shifted the garrison to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Kang, Yu Yi’s Jingzhou portfolio moved its forward base upriver to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 其後秦雍流人多南出樊沔，孝武始於襄陽僑立雍州，仍立京兆、始平、扶風、河南、廣平、義成、北河南七郡，並屬襄陽。

translations.literal: Afterward Qin-Yong refugees mostly went south out of Fan-Mian; Emperor Xiaowu first at Xiangyang established a migrant Yongzhou, and still set up Jingzhao, Shiping, Fufeng, Henan, Guangping, Yicheng, Northern Henan—seven commanderies—and all belonged to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later waves fleeing Qin and Yong spilled through Fan and Mian; Emperor Xiaowu answered by planting a shadow Yongzhou in Xiangyang alongside seven satellite commanderies—Jingzhao, Shiping, Fufeng, Henan, Guangping, Yicheng, and northern Henan—all reporting to the same southern hub.

translations.literal: Xiangyang formerly belonged to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang had long been a Jingzhou town before this layered administration.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢雍州之西界，周衰，其地爲狄。

translations.literal: According to the western border of Yongzhou in Yugong, when Zhou declined, that ground became Di.
translations.idiomatic: The Yugong atlas draws Yongzhou’s western edge across ground that, once Zhou authority frayed, fell to Di pastoralists.

sentences.zh: 秦興美陽甘泉宮，本匈奴鑄金人祭天之處。

translations.literal: The Qin raised Ganquan Palace at Meiyang; originally it was where the Xiongnu cast metal men to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qin builders raised Ganquan Palace near Meiyang atop a Xiongnu altar where great bronze effigies once received skyward offerings.

sentences.zh: 匈奴既失甘泉，又使休屠、渾邪王等居涼州之地。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu having lost Ganquan, also made kings Xiutu, Hunxie, and others dwell in the territory of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of Ganquan, the confederation resettled the Xiutu and Hunye kings and their followings across what would become Liangzhou pasture.

sentences.zh: 二王後以地降漢，漢置張掖、酒泉、敦煌、武威郡。

translations.literal: The two kings afterward with the land surrendered to Han; Han established Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, Wuwei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Those two kings eventually yielded their ranges to Han, which organized the corridor into Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 其後又置金城郡，謂之河西五郡。

translations.literal: Afterward Jincheng Commandery was also established; it was called the Hexi five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng was added later, completing the famous pentad of Hexi commanderies.

sentences.zh: 漢改周之雍州爲涼州，蓋以地處西方，常寒涼也。

translations.literal: Han changed Zhou’s Yongzhou into Liangzhou; presumably because the ground lies in the west and is constantly cold-cool.
translations.idiomatic: Han mapmakers retired Zhou’s Yongzhou label for the west in favor of Liangzhou—cold frontier, high sky, wind that never quite warms.

sentences.zh: 地勢西北邪出，在南山之間，南隔西羌，西通西域，于時號爲斷匈奴右臂。

translations.literal: The terrain trends northwest out between southern mountains, south separated from western Qiang, west connecting to western regions; at the time it was called severing the Xiongnu’s right arm.
translations.idiomatic: The corridor runs northwest between southern ranges, screens the Qiang on one flank and opens toward the Tarim on the other; strategists called it cleaving the Xiongnu’s sword arm.

sentences.zh: 獻帝時，涼州數有亂，河西五郡去州隔遠，於是乃別以爲雍州。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xian, Liangzhou repeatedly had disorder; the Hexi five commanderies were distant separated from the province; thereupon they separately treated it as Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian’s reign saw Liangzhou convulsed so often that the five Hexi prefectures, sundered from the provincial seat, were hived off as a separate Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 末又依古典定九州，乃合關右以爲雍州。

translations.literal: In the end again according to ancient canon the nine provinces were fixed; then Guanyou was combined to be Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han surveyors, nostalgic for the ninefold Yugong grid, folded the entire Guanyou plateau back into a single Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏時復分以爲涼州，刺史領戊己校尉，護西域，如漢故事，至晉不改。

translations.literal: In Wei times it was again split to be Liangzhou; the governor concurrently held the wuji colonel, protected the western regions, according to Han precedent; down to Jin it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei restored a stand-alone Liangzhou whose governors, like their Han forebears, doubled as wuji colonels shepherding the Western Regions—a practice Jin left untouched.

sentences.zh: 統郡八，縣四十六，戶三萬七百。

translations.literal: It governed eight commanderies, forty-six counties, households thirty thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The province embraced eight commanderies, forty-six counties, and thirty thousand seven hundred households.

translations.literal: Jincheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Founded in the Han expansion wave.〉

translations.literal: It governed five counties; households two thousand.〉
translations.idiomatic: Five counties and two thousand households fell within its boundary.〉

sentences.zh: 榆中 允街 金城 白土 浩亹

translations.literal: Yuzhong, Yunjie, Jincheng, Baitu, Haomen.
translations.idiomatic: Its seats included Yuzhong, Yunjie, Jincheng, Baitu, and Haomen.

translations.literal: Xiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiping commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Another Han foundation.〉

translations.literal: It governed four counties; households four thousand.〉
translations.idiomatic: Four counties and four thousand households stood on its registers.〉

sentences.zh: 西都 臨羌 長寧 安夷

translations.literal: Xidu, Linqiang, Changning, Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xidu, Linqiang, Changning, and Anyi counties.

translations.literal: Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Organized under Han to seal the corridor.〉

translations.literal: It governed seven counties; households five thousand nine hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Seven counties and five thousand nine hundred households answered to it.〉

sentences.zh: 姑臧 宣威 揖次 倉松 顯美 驪靬 番和

translations.literal: Guzang, Xuanwei, Yici, Cangsong, Xianmei, Liqian, Fanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Guzang served as principal seat alongside Xuanwei, Yici, Cangsong, Xianmei, Liqian, and Fanhe.

translations.literal: Zhangye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangye commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Han-era placement.〉

translations.literal: It governed three counties; households three thousand seven hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Three counties carried three thousand seven hundred households.〉

translations.literal: Yongping, Linze.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping and Linze counties.

translations.literal: 〈Under Han it was Zhaowu County; it was changed to avoid Emperor Wen’s taboo.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Formerly Han’s Zhaowu county, renamed Yongping to dodge Wen-di’s personal name.〉

translations.literal: Wulan.
translations.idiomatic: Wulan County.

translations.literal: 〈Han followed the Wulan name.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Han registrars kept the older Wulan toponym.〉

translations.literal: Western Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Xijun or western commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yet another Han-line commandery.〉

translations.literal: It governed five counties; households one thousand nine hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: It claimed five counties and nearly two thousand households.〉

sentences.zh: 日勒 刪丹 仙提 萬歲 蘭池

translations.literal: Rile, Shandan, Xianti, Wansui, Lanci.
translations.idiomatic: Rile, Shandan, Xianti, Wansui, and Lanci lined its map.

translations.literal: 〈One version says Lanjue Pool.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Some glosses read the marsh as Lanjue Pool.〉

translations.literal: Jiuquan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuquan commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Han founded it to anchor the middle corridor.〉

translations.literal: It governed nine counties; households four thousand four hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Nine counties mustered four thousand four hundred households.〉

sentences.zh: 福祿 會水 安彌 騂馬 樂涫 表氏 延壽 玉門 沙頭

translations.literal: Fulu, Huishui, Anmi, Xingma, Legu, Biaoshi, Yanshou, Yumen, Shatou.
translations.idiomatic: Fulu, Huishui, Anmi, Xingma, Legu, Biaoshi, Yanshou, Yumen, and Shatou completed the roll.

translations.literal: Dunhuang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dunhuang commandery.

translations.literal: 〈The Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Han’s westernmost prefecture in the corridor.〉

translations.literal: It governed twelve counties; households six thousand three hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Twelve counties housed six thousand three hundred households.〉

sentences.zh: 昌蒲 敦煌 龍勒 陽關 效穀 廣至 宜禾 冥安[32]深泉[33]伊吾 新鄉 乾齊

translations.literal: Changpu, Dunhuang, Longle, Yangguan, Xiaogu, Guangzhi, Yihe, Ming’an, Shenquan, Yiwu, Xinxiang, Ganqi.
translations.idiomatic: Changpu, Dunhuang, Longle, Yangguan, Xiaogu, Guangzhi, Yihe, Ming’an, Shenquan, Yiwu, Xinxiang, and Ganqi formed its dozen seats.

translations.literal: West Sea Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Xihai or west-sea commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈故屬張掖，漢獻帝興平二年，武威太守張雅請置。

translations.literal: 〈Formerly belonging to Zhangye; in the second year of Emperor Xian of Han’s Xingping era, Wuwei Governor Zhang Ya requested its establishment.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Spun out of Zhangye after Wuwei prefect Zhang Ya petitioned Emperor Xian during Xingping’s second year.〉

translations.literal: It governed one county; households two thousand five hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: A lone county still counted two thousand five hundred households.〉

translations.literal: Juyan.
translations.idiomatic: The Juyan salient.

translations.literal: 〈The marsh is southeast; this is what the Documents calls flowing sands.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Southeast lay the reed sea, the “flowing sands” of the Shangshu imagination.〉

sentences.zh: 元康五年，惠帝分敦煌郡之宜禾、伊吾、冥安、深泉、廣至等五縣，分酒泉之沙頭縣，又別立會稽、新鄉，凡八縣爲晉昌郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuankang, Emperor Hui split from Dunhuang Commandery the five counties Yihe, Yiwu, Ming’an, Shenquan, Guangzhi; split from Jiuquan Shatou County; also separately established Kuaiji, Xinxiang; altogether eight counties became Jinchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang’s fifth year saw Emperor Hui peel Yihe, Yiwu, Ming’an, Shenquan, and Guangzhi from Dunhuang, lift Shatou from Jiuquan, and mint fresh Kuaiji and Xinxiang registers—eight counties in all under a new Jinchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 永寧中，張軌爲涼州刺史，鎮武威，上表請合秦雍流移人於姑臧西北，置武興郡，統武興、大城、烏支、襄武、晏然、新鄣、平狄、司監等縣。

translations.literal: In Yongning, Zhang Gui was governor of Liangzhou, garrisoned Wuwei, submitted a memorial requesting to combine Qin and Yong refugee migrants northwest of Guzang, set up Wuxing Commandery, governing Wuxing, Dacheng, Wuzhi, Xiangwu, Yanran, Xinzhang, Pingdi, Sijian, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Yongning, Liangzhou governor Zhang Gui, encamped at Wuwei, asked the throne to gather Qin-Yong exiles beyond northwest Guzang into a Wuxing commandery built around seats named Wuxing, Dacheng, Wuzhi, Xiangwu, Yanran, Xinzhang, Pingdi, and Sijian.

sentences.zh: 又分西平界置晉興郡，統晉興、枹罕、永固、臨津、臨鄣、廣昌、大夏、遂興、罕唐、左南等縣。

translations.literal: Also split Xiping’s border to establish Jinxing Commandery, governing Jinxing, Fuhan, Yonggu, Linjin, Linzhang, Guangchang, Daxia, Suixing, Hantang, Zuonan, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise trimmed Xiping to raise Jinxing commandery—seats at Jinxing, Fuhan, Yonggu, Linjin, Linzhang, Guangchang, Daxia, Suixing, Hantang, Zuonan, and more.

sentences.zh: 是時中原淪沒，元帝徙居江左，軌乃控據河西，稱晉正朔，是爲前涼。

translations.literal: At this time the central plain sank and was lost; Emperor Yuan moved to dwell left of the Yangtze; Gui then controlled and held Hexi, claiming Jin’s correct calendar; this was Former Liang.
translations.idiomatic: While the Central Plains drowned in war and Emperor Yuan beached his court south of the great river, Zhang Gui clasped the Hexi corridor, flew Jin’s banner, and so founded what historians call Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 及張寔，分金城之令居、枝陽二縣，又立永登縣，合三縣立廣武郡。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Zhang Shi, he divided Lingju and Zhiyang, the two counties of Jincheng, also established Yongdeng County, and with the three counties together established Guangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Shi, Lingju and Zhiyang—two counties carved from Jincheng—were joined with newly founded Yongdeng, and the trio became Guangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 張茂分武興、金城、西平、安故爲定州。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao divided Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu to be Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao formed Ding Province from Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu.

sentences.zh: 張駿分武威、武興、西平、張掖、酒泉、建康、西海、西郡、湟河、晉興、廣武合十一郡爲涼州，[34]興晉、金城、武始、南安、永晉、大夏、武成、漢中爲河州，敦煌、晉昌、高昌、西域都護、戊己校尉、玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun divided Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu—eleven commanderies in all—to be Liang Province; Xingjin, Jincheng, Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong to be He Province; Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, the Protector-General of the Western Regions, the Colonel of Wuji, and the Grand Protector of Yumen—three commanderies and three camps—to be Sha Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun organized Liang Province out of eleven commanderies: Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu. He drew He Province from Xingjin, Jincheng, Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong. Sha Province bundled Dunhuang, Jinchang, and Gaochang with the Western Regions protectorate, the Wuji colonelcy, and the Yumen grand protectorate—three civil jurisdictions and three encampments.

translations.literal: Zhang Jun held in acting capacity the governorship of Liang Province and administered three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun served as acting governor-general of Liang and held all three provinces in his portfolio.

sentences.zh: 張祚又以敦煌郡爲商州。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo again took Dunhuang Commandery and made it Shang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo turned Dunhuang Commandery into Shang Province.

sentences.zh: 永興中，置漢陽縣以守牧地，張玄靚改爲祁連郡。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era, Hanyang County was established to guard pasturelands; Zhang Xuanjing changed it to Qilian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Yongxing saw Hanyang County founded to watch the grazing country; Zhang Xuanjing later elevated the district to Qilian Commandery.

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi again separately established Linsong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi added an independent Linsong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 天錫降於苻氏，其地尋爲呂光所據。

translations.literal: Tianxi surrendered to the Fu; the territory was soon taken by Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianxi yielded to the Fu house, Lü Guang seized the ground almost at once.

sentences.zh: 呂光都於姑臧後，以郭黁言讖，改昌松爲東張掖郡。

translations.literal: After Lü Guang made his capital at Guzang, because of Guo Nen’s prophecy talk, he changed Changsong to Eastern Zhangye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Guang ruled from Guzang, a prophecy uttered by Guo Nen moved him to rename Changsong Eastern Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 及呂隆降於姚興，其地三分。

translations.literal: When Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing, the territory was divided three ways.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long’s submission to Yao Xing left the realm split among three claimants.

sentences.zh: 武昭王爲西涼，建號於敦煌。

translations.literal: King Wuzhao became Western Liang and established his title at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wuzhao founded Western Liang, raising his banner at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤爲南涼，建號於樂都。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu became Southern Liang and established his title at Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu proclaimed Southern Liang with his seat at Ledu.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜爲北涼，建號於張掖。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun became Northern Liang and established his title at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun forged Northern Liang, enthroned in spirit at Zhangye.

translations.literal: And they divided and occupied five commanderies of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Between them they partitioned the five Hexi commanderies.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢本雍州之域，魏始分隴右置焉，刺史領護羌校尉，中間暫廢。

translations.literal: According to the Tribute of Yu it was originally within Yong Province; Wei first divided Longyou and set it up; the inspector also bore the title Colonel Protecting the Qiang; in between it was briefly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The classic text places this land in old Yong. Wei first peeled Longyou away as a province whose governor doubled as Colonel Protecting the Qiang, though the office flickered out for a time midstream.

sentences.zh: 及泰始五年，又以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平，合七郡置秦州，鎮冀城。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Taishi, again with five commanderies of Longyou from Yong Province together with Jincheng of Hexi Liang Province and Yinping of the Liang Province in the south—seven commanderies in all—Qin Province was established, garrisoned at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 5, Yong’s five Longyou commanderies, Jincheng from the northwestern Liang, and Yinping from the southern Liang—seven units altogether—were folded into a revived Qin Province headquartered at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 太康三年，罷秦州，并雍州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taikang, Qin Province was abolished and merged into Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 3 abolished Qin Province and swallowed it back into Yong.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, it was re-established, garrisoned at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh year saw it rise again, now anchored at Shanggui.

translations.literal: Emperor Hui divided Didao, Lintao, and Heguan from Longxi, and further founded Taoyang, Suiping, Wujie, Shixing, Diwu, and Zhenqiu—six counties—nine counties in all—to establish Didao Commandery, subordinate to Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui peeled Didao, Lintao, and Heguan out of Longxi, minted six new counties—Taoyang, Suiping, Wujie, Shixing, Diwu, and Zhenqiu—and grouped all nine into a new Didao Commandery under Qin.

sentences.zh: 張駿分屬涼州，又以狄道縣立武始郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun assigned it to Liang Province and used Didao County to establish Wushi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun shifted the unit to Liang’s orbit and made Didao County the core of a fresh Wushi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 江左分梁爲秦，寄居梁州，又立氐池爲北秦州。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi they divided Liang to form Qin, lodging it within Liang Province, and also established Dichi as Northern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Across the river the court carved a shadow Qin from Liang, parked it inside Liang Province for administration, and raised Dichi as Northern Qin.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢華陽黑水之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。

translations.literal: According to the Tribute of Yu it is the land of Huayang and the Blackwater; Shun established twelve shepherds, and this was one.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute of Yu draws this terrain between Huayang and the Blackwater, one of the twelve pastures Shun entrusted to his herdsmen.

sentences.zh: 梁者，言西方金剛之氣強梁，故因名焉。

translations.literal: As for Liang: it means the hard metal qi of the west was strong and overbearing, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The name Liang speaks of the western edge’s stern, metallic vigor—unyielding force—crystallized in a single word.

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Director of Regions annexed Liang to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou ritual canon had the cartographer fold Liang into Yong.

sentences.zh: 漢不立州名，以其地爲益州。

translations.literal: Han did not establish a provincial name; it treated the territory as Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han never titled the region a zhou of its own; everything here counted as Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平六年，[38]以臨江縣屬永寧郡。

translations.literal: By Emperor Xian’s sixth year of Chuping, Linjiang County belonged to Yongning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Emperor Xian’s Chuping reign, Linjiang County was folded under Yongning.

sentences.zh: 建安六年，劉璋改永寧爲巴東郡，分巴郡墊江置巴西郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jian'an, Liu Zhang changed Yongning to Badong Commandery and split Dianjiang from Ba Commandery to establish Baxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 6 saw Liu Zhang rename Yongning as Badong and spin Dianjiang out of Ba to seed Baxi.

sentences.zh: 劉備據蜀，又分廣漢之葭萌、涪城、梓潼、白水四縣，改葭萌曰漢壽，又立漢德縣，以爲梓潼郡；

translations.literal: Liu Bei held Shu and again divided Jiameng, Fucheng, Zitong, and Baishui—four counties from Guanghan—renaming Jiameng to Hanshou, also establishing Hande County, making them Zitong Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei seized Shu he carved four Guanghan counties—Jiameng, Fucheng, Zitong, and Baishui—renamed Jiameng Hanshou, added Hande, and drew the lot into Zitong Commandery;

sentences.zh: 割巴郡之宕渠、宣漢、漢昌三縣置宕渠郡，尋省，以縣並屬巴西郡。

translations.literal: he cut Dangqu, Xuanhan, and Hangchang—three counties from Ba Commandery—to establish Dangqu Commandery; soon it was abolished and the counties were all merged into Baxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: he tried to hive Dangqu, Xuanhan, and Hangchang off Ba as Dangqu Commandery, though the experiment was short-lived and those towns soon returned to Baxi.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，分益州，立梁州於漢中，改漢壽爲晉壽，又分廣漢置新都郡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, Yizhou was divided to establish Liang Province at Hanzhong; Hanshou was changed to Jinshou; and Guanghan was again divided to establish Xindu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 3 split Yizhou to seat Liang Province in Hanzhong, retitled Hanshou as Jinshou, and broke another slice from Guanghan for Xindu.
