translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Taikang, Xindu Commandery was abolished and merged into Guanghan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, Taikang 6: Xindu Commandery vanished into Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 惠帝復分巴西置宕渠郡，統宕渠、漢昌、宣漢三縣，并以新城、魏興、上庸合四郡以屬梁州。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui again divided Baxi Commandery to establish Dangqu Commandery, governing Dangqu, Hangchang, and Xuanhan—three counties—and together with Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong—four commanderies in all—made them belong to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui peeled Baxi again to resurrect Dangqu over three counties, then yoked that package with Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong—four commanderies—to Liang.

sentences.zh: 尋而梁州郡縣沒于李特，永嘉中又分屬楊茂搜，其晉人流寓於梁益者，仍於二州立南北二陰平郡。

translations.literal: Soon the commanderies and counties of Liang Province fell to Li Te; in the Yongjia era they were again portioned to Yang Maosou; as for Jin people wandering in Liang and Yi, they still established northern and southern Yinping Commanderies on the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s map soon washed into Li Te’s hands; Yongjia saw pieces fall to Yang Maosou; Jin exiles caught between Liang and Yi kept stringing up paired Yinping commanderies, north and south.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫平蜀之後，以巴漢流人立晉昌郡，領長樂、安晉、延壽、安樂、宣漢、寧都、新興、吉陽、東關、永安十縣；

translations.literal: After Huan Wen pacified Shu, with refugees from Ba and Han he established Jinchang Commandery, overseeing Changle, Anjin, Yanshou, Anle, Xuanhan, Ningdu, Xinxing, Jiyang, Dongguan, and Yong'an—ten counties;
translations.idiomatic: Once Huan Wen stilled Shu, he settled Ba-Han refugees in a new Jinchang Commandery spanning ten counties: Changle, Anjin, Yanshou, Anle, Xuanhan, Ningdu, Xinxing, Jiyang, Dongguan, and Yong'an;

sentences.zh: 又置益昌、晉興二縣，屬巴西郡；

translations.literal: he also placed Yichang and Jinxing—two counties—under Baxi Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: he tucked Yichang and Jinxing under Baxi as well;

sentences.zh: 於德陽界東南置遂寧郡；

translations.literal: in the southeast within the bounds of Deyang he established Suining Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: and along Deyang’s southeast marches he opened Suining Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又於晉壽置劍閣縣，屬梁州。

translations.literal: Again at Jinshou establish Jiange county, subordinate to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They also founded Jiange County at Jinshou and placed it under Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 後孝武分梓潼北界立晉壽郡，統晉壽、白水、邵歡、興安四縣；

translations.literal: Later Xiaowu divide Zitong north border establish Jinshou commandery, govern Jinshou, Baishui, Shaohuan, Xing'an four counties;
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowu carved the northern rim of Zitong into Jinshou Commandery, which ruled the four counties of Jinshou, Baishui, Shaohuan, and Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 梓潼郡徙居梓潼，罷劍閣縣；

translations.literal: Zitong commandery move reside Zitong, abolish Jiange county;
translations.idiomatic: The seat of Zitong Commandery was shifted to Zitong proper, and Jiange County was abolished.

sentences.zh: 又別置南漢中郡，分巴西、梓潼爲金山郡。

translations.literal: Again separately establish Nanhanzhong commandery, divide Baxi, Zitong make Jinshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Nanhanzhong Commandery was also established, and lands taken from Baxi and Zitong were gathered into Jinshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及安帝時，又立新巴、汶陽二郡，又有北新巴、華陽、南陰平、北陰平四郡，其後又立巴渠、懷安、宋熙、白水、上洛、北上洛、南宕渠、懷漢、新興、安康等十郡。

translations.literal: Reach Emperor An time, again establish Xinba, Wenyang two commanderies, again have Beixinba, Huayang, Nan Yinping, Bei Yinping four commanderies, afterward again establish Baqu, Huai'an, Songxi, Baishui, Shangluo, Beishangluo, Nan Dangqu, Huaihan, Xinxing, Ankang etcetera ten commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An the court added Xinba and Wenyang, followed by four more—Northern Xinba, Huayang, Southern Yinping, and Northern Yinping—and later founded another ten, among them Baqu, Huai'an, Songxi, Baishui, Shangluo, Northern Shangluo, Southern Dangqu, Huaihan, Xinxing, and Ankang.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢及舜十二牧俱爲梁州之域，周合梁於雍，則又爲雍州之地。

translations.literal: Examine Yugong and Shun twelve shepherds all be Liangzhou territory, Zhou combine Liang in Yong, then again be Yongzhou land.
translations.idiomatic: The "Tribute of Yu" and the twelve shepherds of Shun alike mapped this country inside Liang Province; when the Zhou folded Liang into Yong, the same hills and rivers became territory of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「參伐流爲益州，益之爲言阨也。

translations.literal: "Chunqiu Yuanming Bao" says: "Shen Fa flow become Yizhou, Yi speak choke/narrow.
translations.idiomatic: The *Chunqiu Yuanming Bao* says: "The constellation of Shen and Fa spilled their light downward to become Yizhou; the syllable *yi* is a word for straitened defiles."

sentences.zh: 」言其所在之地險阨也，亦曰疆壤益大，故以名焉。

translations.literal: " say its located place dangerous narrow, also say border soil increasingly great, therefore with name therein.
translations.idiomatic: "—in other words, its ground is perilous and tight hemmed—and some also say its frontiers ever widened, which is why the name took hold."

sentences.zh: 始秦惠王滅蜀，置郡，以張若爲蜀守。

translations.literal: Begin Qin Huiwang destroy Shu, establish commandery, use Zhang Ruo as Shu governor.
translations.idiomatic: When King Hui of Qin extinguished Shu, he laid out a commandery and named Zhang Ruo its governor.

sentences.zh: 及始皇置三十六郡，蜀郡之名不改。

translations.literal: Reach First Emperor establish thirty-six commanderies, Shu commandery name not change.
translations.idiomatic: Once the First Emperor fixed the realm at thirty-six commanderies, the old name Shu Commandery still stood.

translations.literal: Han beginning have Hanzhong, Ba, Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding years of Han the southwest still answered to Hanzhong, Ba, and Shu.

sentences.zh: 高祖六年，分蜀置廣漢，凡爲四郡。

translations.literal: Gaozu sixth year, divide Shu establish Guanghan, altogether be four commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Gaozu's reign, Shu was split to create Guanghan, making four commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 武帝開西南夷，更置犍爲、牂柯、越巂、益州四郡，凡八郡，遂置益州統焉，益州蓋始此也。

translations.literal: Wudi open southwest Yi, further establish Qianwei, Zangke, Yuexi, Yizhou four commanderies, altogether eight commanderies, then establish Yizhou govern them, Yizhou probably begin here.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu opened the southwestern tribes and added Qianwei, Zangke, Yuexi, and Yizhou—eight commanderies altogether—then set a Yizhou superintendency above them; the great province of Yizhou, one may say, begins here.

sentences.zh: 及後漢，明帝以新附置永昌郡，安帝又以諸道置蜀、廣漢、犍爲三郡屬國都尉，及靈帝又以汶江、蠶陵、廣柔三縣立汶山郡。

translations.literal: Reach Later Han, Mingdi with new annex establish Yongchang commandery, Andi again with various roads establish Shu, Guanghan, Qianwei three commandery dependent-state commandants, reach Lingdi again with Wenjiang, Canling, Guangrou three counties establish Wenshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han, Mingdi carved Yongchang from fresh conquests; Andi appointed commandants for dependent states attached to Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei; and Lingdi raised Wenshan Commandery from the three counties of Wenjiang, Canling, and Guangrou.

sentences.zh: 獻帝初平元年，劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡。

translations.literal: Xiandi Chuping first year, Liu Zhang divide Ba commandery establish Yongning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Chuping year of Emperor Xian, Liu Zhang broke Yongning Commandery out of Ba.

sentences.zh: [42]建安六年，改永寧爲巴東，以巴郡爲巴西，又立涪陵郡。

translations.literal: Jian'an sixth year, change Yongning be Badong, take Ba commandery be Baxi, again establish Fuling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jian'an, Yongning became Badong, the old Ba Commandery was renamed Baxi, and Fuling Commandery was founded besides.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，劉備分巴郡立固陵郡。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year, Liu Bei divide Ba commandery establish Guling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the same reign arc, Liu Bei set Guling Commandery apart from Ba.

sentences.zh: 蜀章武元年又改固陵爲巴東郡，巴西郡爲巴郡，又分廣漢立梓潼郡，分犍爲立江陽郡，以蜀郡屬國爲漢嘉郡，以犍爲屬國爲朱提郡。

translations.literal: Shu Zhangwu first year again change Guling be Badong commandery, Baxi commandery be Ba commandery, again divide Guanghan establish Zitong commandery, divide Qianwei establish Jiangyang commandery, take Shu commandery dependent-state be Hanjia commandery, take Qianwei dependent-state be Zhuti commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Zhangwu year of Shu, Guling was rechristened Badong, Baxi reverted to Ba, Zitong rose from a partition of Guanghan, Jiangyang from Qianwei, the Shu dependent state became Hanjia Commandery, and the Qianwei dependent state became Zhuti Commandery.

sentences.zh: 劉禪建興二年，改益州郡爲建寧郡，廣漢屬國爲陰平郡，分建寧永昌立雲南郡，分建寧牂柯立興古郡，分廣漢立東廣漢郡。

translations.literal: Liu Shan Jianxing second year, change Yizhou commandery be Jianning commandery, Guanghan dependent-state be Yinping commandery, divide Jianning Yongchang establish Yunnan commandery, divide Jianning Zangke establish Xingu commandery, divide Guanghan establish Dong Guanghan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Liu Shan's second Jianxing year, Yizhou Commandery was renamed Jianning, the Guanghan dependent state became Yinping, Yunnan was formed from Jianning and Yongchang, Xingu from Jianning and Zangke, and Eastern Guanghan from a further cut of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 魏景元中，蜀平，省東廣漢郡。

translations.literal: Wei Jingyuan middle, Shu pacified, reduce Dong Guanghan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Wei's Jingyuan era, after Shu had been subdued, Eastern Guanghan Commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 及武帝泰始二年，分益州置梁州，以漢中屬焉。

translations.literal: Reach Wudi Taishi second year, divide Yizhou establish Liangzhou, with Hanzhong belong thereto.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Tai shi year of Emperor Wu, Liang Province was severed from Yizhou, and Hanzhong was transferred to the new division.

translations.literal: Seventh year, again divide Yizhou establish Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later, another share of Yizhou was reassembled into Ning Province.

translations.literal: Emperor Hui after, Li Te usurp title at Shu, call Han, Yizhou commanderies counties all sink in Te.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui's day, Li Te seized a kingly style in Shu, styled his polity Han, and every commandery and county of Yizhou slid beneath his banner.

sentences.zh: 李雄又分漢嘉、蜀二郡立沈黎、漢原二郡。

translations.literal: Li Xiong again divide Hanjia, Shu two commanderies establish Shenli, Hanyuan two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong next split Hanjia and Shu to raise the paired commanderies of Shenli and Hanyuan.

sentences.zh: 是時益州郡縣雖沒李氏，江左並遙置之。

translations.literal: This time Yizhou commanderies counties although sink Li clan, Jiangzuo together distantly place them.
translations.idiomatic: Even while Li's line held the Yizhou registers, the court east of the Yangtze kept naming officials to those posts from afar.

sentences.zh: 桓溫滅蜀，其地復爲晉有，省漢原、沈黎而立南陰平、晉原、寧蜀、始寧四郡焉。

translations.literal: Huan Wen destroy Shu, its land again be Jin have, reduce Hanyuan, Shenli and establish Nan Yinping, Jinyuan, Ningshu, Shining four commanderies therein.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen crushed Shu, the soil returned to Jin, which struck Hanyuan and Shenli from the map and planted four fresh commanderies—Southern Yinping, Jinyuan, Ningshu, and Shining—in their place.

sentences.zh: 咸安二年，益州復沒於苻氏。

translations.literal: Xian'an second year, Yizhou again sink at Fu clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Xian'an year Yizhou sank once more under the Fu dynasty of Former Qin.

translations.literal: Taiyuan eighth year, again be Jin have.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth year of Taiyuan it belonged to Jin again.

sentences.zh: 隆安二年，又立晉熙、遂寧、晉寧三郡云。

translations.literal: Long'an second year, again establish Jinxi, Suining, Jinning three commanderies cloud.
translations.idiomatic: The second Long'an year reportedly saw the founding of Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning commanderies.

translations.literal: At Han Wei be Yizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Across Han and Wei this had been heartland of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，武帝以益州地廣，分益州之建寧、興古、雲南、交州之永昌，合四郡爲寧州，統縣四十五，戶八萬三千。

translations.literal: Taishi seventh year, Wudi because Yizhou land broad, divide Yizhou Jianning, Xingu, Yunnan, Jiaozhou Yongchang, combine four commanderies be Ningzhou, govern counties forty-five, households 83,000.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh Taishi year, Emperor Wu judged Yizhou too sprawling and folded Jianning, Xingu, and Yunnan from it together with Yongchang out of Jiaozhou—four commanderies—to constitute Ning Province, with forty-five counties and eighty-three thousand households on its books.

translations.idiomatic: Its counties were Buwei, Yongshou, Bisu, Yongxiang, Nanfu, Suitang, Ailao, and Bonan.

sentences.zh: 太康三年，武帝又廢寧州入益州，立南夷校尉以護之。

translations.literal: Taikang third year, Wudi again abolish Ningzhou enter Yizhou, establish Nan Yi colonel to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang three, Emperor Wu abolished Ning Province and folded it back into Yizhou, creating a Colonel of the Southern Tribes to watch over the frontier.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，惠帝復置寧州，又分建寧以西七縣別立爲益州郡。

translations.literal: Tai'an second year, Huidi again establish Ningzhou, again divide Jianning west seven counties separately establish be Yizhou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an two saw Emperor Hui revive Ning Province and peel seven counties west of Jianning into a stand-alone Yizhou Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年，改益州郡曰晉寧，分牂柯立平夷、夜郎二郡。

translations.literal: Yongjia second year, change Yizhou commandery say Jinning, divide Zangke establish Pingyi, Yelang two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Yongjia year Yizhou Commandery was rebaptized Jinning, while Pingyi and Yelang were broken out of Zangke.

translations.literal: Yet this time its land again be Li Te possess.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ground had once more slipped into Li Te's grasp.

sentences.zh: 其後李壽分寧州興古、永昌、雲南、朱提、越巂、河陽六郡爲漢州。

translations.literal: Afterward Li Shou divide Ningzhou Xingu, Yongchang, Yunnan, Zhuti, Yuexi, Heyang six commanderies be Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Shou drafted six commanderies—Xingu, Yongchang, Yunnan, Zhuti, Yuexi, and Heyang—from Ning Province to constitute Han Province.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，分牂柯、夜郎、朱提、越巂四郡置安州。

translations.literal: Xiankang fourth year, divide Zangke, Yelang, Zhuti, Yuexi four commanderies establish Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth Xiankang year established An Province from the four commanderies of Zangke, Yelang, Zhuti, and Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 八年，又罷并寧州，以越巂還屬益州，省永昌郡焉。

translations.literal: Eighth year, again abolish merge Ningzhou, with Yuexi return belong Yizhou, reduce Yongchang commandery therein.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years on, An was rescinded and merged back into Ning Province, Yuexi was returned to Yizhou's orbit, and Yongchang Commandery vanished from the rolls.

translations.literal: Collation record
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 崆山訪道「崆」，宋本、局本等作「風」，殿本作「崆」，今從殿本。

translations.literal: Kong mountain seek way 'Kong', Song edition, bureau edition etcetera write 'Feng', Palace edition write 'Kong', now follow Palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: For the character read *kong* in the phrase about seeking the Way on Mount Kong, Song and bureau imprints have *wind*, whereas the Palace woodblock keeps *kong*; this text sides with the Palace edition.

sentences.zh: 黃帝于崆峒山訪道，傳自莊子。

translations.literal: Yellow Emperor at Kongtong mountain seek way, transmit from Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The tale that the Yellow Emperor climbed Kongtong to question the Dao comes down to us through the *Zhuangzi*.

sentences.zh: 義陽據下「武帝增置」之文及「義陽郡」下之文，義陽郡又置于晉武帝太康時。

translations.literal: Yiyang according below 'Wudi add establish' text and 'Yiyang commandery' below text, Yiyang commandery again establish at Jin Wudi Taikang time.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang should be read alongside the phrase "Emperor Wu additionally founded" further down and the body text under "Yiyang Commandery"; together they show Yiyang Commandery was also instituted in Emperor Wu of Jin's Taikang era.

sentences.zh: 永壽三年戶千六十七萬七千九百六十口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六後漢書郡國志在本志校記中以後簡稱《續漢志·一》注云：「永壽二年，戶千六百七萬九百六，口五千六萬六千八百五十六人。」

translations.literal: Yongshou three years households 10,677,960 mouths 56,486,856 Hou Hanshu Jun Guo Zhi in this treatise collation afterward abbreviate 'Xu Han Zhi 1' note says: 'Yongshou two years, households 16,070,906, mouths 56,068,056 people.'
translations.idiomatic: The figures given here for Yongshou three—10,677,960 households and 56,486,856 persons—sit awkwardly beside a gloss in the *Hou Hanshu* "Treatise on Commanderies," cited in these collation notes as *Continuation of Han I*, which records Yongshou two as 16,070,906 households and 56,068,056 people.

sentences.zh: 嗣王之庶子爲亭侯各本無「亭」字，殿本有。

translations.literal: Successor king collateral sons be village marquis each edition lack 'village' character, Palace edition have.
translations.idiomatic: The line calling the successor king's younger sons "village marquises" omits the word *village* in most recensions, but the Palace edition preserves it.

sentences.zh: 今從殿本，與魏志文帝紀合。

translations.literal: Now follow Palace edition, with Wei Zhi Wendi annals match.
translations.idiomatic: The present copy follows the Palace text, which matches the annals of Emperor Wen in the *Wei zhi*.

sentences.zh: 位望隆于牧伯「隆」，各本作「降」，宋本作「隆」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Rank reputation high at shepherds elders 'high', each edition write 'descend', Song edition write 'high', now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: Where the line says rank and renown *rose* above regional lords, common editions misprint *fell*; the Song imprint preserves *rose*, and this edition adopts Song.

sentences.zh: 縣一百戶四十七萬五千七百下所列爲縣九十九，戶四十九萬二千四百。

translations.literal: Counties one hundred households 475,700 below listed be counties ninety-nine, households 492,400.
translations.idiomatic: The rubric announces one hundred counties and 475,700 households, yet the roster beneath counts ninety-nine counties and 492,400 households.

sentences.zh: 兩數不合，各州頗有此類情況，以後不具校。

translations.literal: Two numbers not match, each province rather have this kind situation, afterward not fully collate.
translations.idiomatic: The tallies disagree; many provinces show the same pattern, and later cases will not be exhaustively collated.

sentences.zh: 有博浪長沙張良擊秦始皇處 畢沅《晉書·地理志·新補正》

translations.literal: Have Bolang Changsha Zhang Liang strike Qin First Emperor place Bi Yuan "Jin Shu Di Li Zhi Xin Bu Zheng"
translations.idiomatic: The gloss marking Bolang as the place where Zhang Liang of Changsha ambushed the First Emperor appears in Bi Yuan's *New Corrections to the Jin shu Treatise on Geography*.

translations.literal: (Below abbreviate call 'Bi Jiao')
translations.idiomatic: (Hereafter abbreviated as *Bi Jiao*.)

sentences.zh: 謂「遍檢諸地志，皆云博浪沙在陽武。

translations.literal: Say "everywhere examine various geographical gazetteers, all say Bolangsha at Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: There he argues that "after combing every geographical handbook, all agree Bolangsha lies in Yangwu."

sentences.zh: 」疑此十二字注本在「陽武」下，錯簡入卷縣耳。

translations.literal: The line begins with a closing quotation mark; editors suspect this twelve-graph note original was beneath “Yangwu,” and a misplaced slip found its way into the counties fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: That gloss properly belongs under “Yangwu”; a strip of bamboo has been bound out of place and landed here among the county entries.

sentences.zh: 分京兆南部置「部」，各本作「郡」，宋本作「部」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Divide Jingzhao south portion establish “bu”; various editions read “jun”; Song edition reads “bu”; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: Where the text carves off the southern half of Jingzhao to erect a “department,” other witnesses print “commandery,” but the Song printing preserves “department,” and that is the reading we adopt.

sentences.zh: 汾陽公國相 《畢校》及方愷《新校·晉書·地理志》

translations.literal: Fenyang duke-state minister: Bi’s Collation and Fang Kai’s New Collation Jin shu Treatise on Geography.
translations.idiomatic: On Fenyang and the chancellor of the princely fief, consult Bi Yuan’s collation and Fang Kai’s New Collation of the Jin shu’s chapter on geography.

translations.literal: (Below abbreviated “Fang’s Collation.”)
translations.idiomatic: (Hereafter cited as Fang’s Collation.)

translations.literal: Both say “Fenyang” ought be read as “Fenyin.”
translations.idiomatic: Both authorities agree that “Fenyang” should in fact read “Fenyin.”

sentences.zh: 按：「公國相」，各本作「公相國」，「相國」二字誤倒，宋本不誤，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Comment: “duke-state minister,” various editions read “duke minister-duke-state,” graphs “minister-state” wrongly inverted; Song edition not wrong; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase should be “chancellor of the ducal state”; witnesses transpose two characters into the meaningless “chancellor of state of the duke.” The Song exemplar preserves the correct order, and we follow it.

sentences.zh: 清泉考異：本「清淵」，避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Qingquan variant: originally “Qingyuan”; changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Qingquan: the underlying form was “Qingyuan,” with “abyss” masked to honor a Tang imperial name.

sentences.zh: 大戚考異：大戚即廣戚，隋避煬帝諱改。

translations.literal: Daqi variant: Daqi is Guangqi; Sui avoided Yangdi taboo and changed.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi is only Guangqi under another brush-stroke meant to skirt the taboo on a Sui emperor’s given name.

sentences.zh: 兗端也「端」，各本作「瑞」，今從宋本作「端」。

translations.literal: Yan duan particle “duan,” various editions read “rui”; now follow Song edition as “duan.”
translations.idiomatic: In the passage on Yan that hinges on the graph “end,” other editions substitute the homophone for “auspicious omen”; we keep the Song reading “end.”

sentences.zh: 魏武帝封考異：袁廷檮曰，「武帝」當作「元帝」，即常道鄉公也。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu enfeoffment variant: Yuan Tingtao says “Emperor Wu” ought read “Emperor Yuan,” namely duke of Changdaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On Wei’s bestowal of rank: Yuan Tingtao argues that “Emperor Wu” must be “Emperor Yuan,” the young puppet styled duke of Changdao township.

translations.literal: Jin received abdication, enfeoffed him Chenliu king.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin took the mandate by abdication, he was invested as prince of Chenliu.

translations.literal: Jiyin commandery original text read “Jiyang commandery.”
translations.idiomatic: The treatise first said “Jiyang commandery” where it should name Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 考異：漢無濟陽郡，蓋「濟陰」之誤。

translations.literal: Variant: Han had no Jiyang commandery; probably “Jiyin’s” error.
translations.idiomatic: Commentarial note: the Han never had a Jiyang commandery; “Jiyang” is almost certainly a scribal slip for Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 卞壺傳濟陰冤句人，宋書州郡志於城武、離狐二縣並云晉太康地志屬濟陰。

translations.literal: Bi Gun biography Jiyin Yuanqu person; Song shu treatise on provinces at Chengwu, Lihu two counties both say Jin Taikang geography belonged Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gun’s biography calls him a native of Yuanqu in Jiyin, and the Song shu’s gazetteer notes for both Chengwu and Lihu cite the Jin Taikang geography to show they lay within Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 按：《左傳》隱公七年杜注及郤詵傳並可證。

translations.literal: Comment: Zuo zhuan Duke Yin seventh year Du annotation and Xi Shen biography both can verify.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu’s gloss on the seventh year of Duke Yin in the Zuo zhuan, together with Xi Shen’s biography, corroborate the point.

translations.literal: Now according change.
translations.idiomatic: The text is emended on that evidence.

sentences.zh: 宛句卞壺傳作「冤句」，《漢書·地理志》在本志校記中以後簡稱漢志上、《續漢志·三》、宋書州郡志在本志校記中以後簡稱宋志一、魏書地形志在本志校記中以後簡稱後魏志二、隋書地理志在本志校記中以後簡稱隋志中並作「冤句」。

translations.literal: Yuanju Bi Gun biography writes “Yuanqu”; Han shu geography, in this treatise’s collation hereafter abbreviated Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 3, Song shu provinces hereafter Song zhi 1, Wei shu terrain hereafter Hou Wei zhi 2, Sui shu geography hereafter Sui zhi zhong all write “Yuanqu.”
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gun’s biography spells the place “Yuanqu,” and the same spelling appears in the Han shu geography (Hanshi shang in these notes), fascicle three of the Continued Han treatise, the Song shu gazetteer (Song zhi 1), the Wei shu terrain chapter (Hou Wei zhi 2), and the Sui shu geography (Sui zhi zhong).

translations.literal: Hulu original text read “Luhu.”
translations.idiomatic: The line originally reversed the order to “Luhu” instead of Hulu.

sentences.zh: 舉正：當作「湖陸」，見《左傳》襄公十九年杜注。

translations.literal: Rectification: ought read “Hulu,” see Zuo zhuan Duke Xiang nineteenth year Du annotation.
translations.idiomatic: It must be Hulu, as Du Yu’s gloss on the nineteenth year of Duke Xiang in the Zuo zhuan shows.

sentences.zh: 斠注：水經濟水、泗水注亦作「湖陸」。

translations.literal: Gloss: Shui jing Ji River, Si River commentaries also write “Hulu.”
translations.idiomatic: Supporting note: the Shui jing’s passages on the Ji and Si rivers likewise record Hulu.

sentences.zh: 按：漢志上、《續漢志·三》謂本曰湖陵，莽改湖陸。

translations.literal: Comment: Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 3 say originally named Huling, Mang changed Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: The upper Han treatise and fascicle three of the Continued Han explain that the place was first called Huling until Wang Mang’s reform renamed it Hulu.

translations.literal: Now according transpose correct.
translations.idiomatic: The characters are transposed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 烏下聚馬與龍晉書地理志注後簡稱馬校：「烏」當作「嶲」。

translations.literal: Wuxia settlement: Ma Yulong’s Jin shu geography commentary, hereafter Ma’s Collation: “wu” ought read “Xi.”
translations.idiomatic: At Wuxia, Ma Yulong’s commentary on the Jin shu geography—cited below as Ma’s Collation—shows the character for “crow” should be read as Xi, the river name.

sentences.zh: 《續漢志·三》作「嶲下聚」，劉昭注引《左傳》僖公二十六年杜注作「嶲下」。

translations.literal: Xu Han zhi 3 writes “Xixia settlement,” Liu Zhao annotation cites Zuo zhuan Duke Xi twenty-sixth year Du annotation writes “Xixia.”
translations.idiomatic: Fascicle three of the Continued Han has Xixia hamlet, and Liu Zhao, citing Du Yu on the twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi, records the same Xixia form.

translations.literal: Nancheng original text read “Nanwucheng.”
translations.idiomatic: The manuscript first read “Nanwucheng” where only Nancheng is meant.

sentences.zh: 考異：景獻羊皇后、惠羊皇后、羊祜傳、宋書羊欣、羊元保傳並云泰山南城人，宋、齊、隋志皆稱南城，惟晉志多一「武」字，殆因下文有「南武陽」而衍一「武」字。

translations.literal: Variant: Empresses Jingxian and Hui of Yang, Yang Hu biography, Song shu Yang Xin, Yang Yuanbao biographies all say Taishan Nancheng person; Song, Qi, Sui gazetteers all call Nancheng; only Jin gazetteer adds one “wu” graph; probably because below text has “Nanwuyang” and duplicated one “wu” graph.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Empresses Jingxian and Hui of the Yang clan, the biography of Yang Hu, and the Song shu lives of Yang Xin and Yang Yuanbao all list them as natives of Nancheng in Taishan; Song, Qi, and Sui gazetteers likewise write Nancheng, whereas the Jin treatise alone inserts an extra “martial,” perhaps because “Nanwuyang” appears just below and the eye slipped.

translations.literal: Comment: Qian’s view correct; now according delete.
translations.idiomatic: Qian’s judgment holds, and the intrusive graph is struck.

translations.literal: Mou original text read “Dongmou.”
translations.idiomatic: The line first read “Dongmou” although the county is simply Mou.

translations.literal: Variant: “east” graph superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: The character “east” is a spurious accretion.

sentences.zh: 漢志上、《續漢志·三》泰山郡有牟縣，即春秋牟國，與東萊之東牟非一地。

translations.literal: Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 3 Taishan commandery has Mou county, namely Spring Autumn Mou state; not same place as Donglai’s Dongmou.
translations.idiomatic: The upper Han treatise and fascicle three of the Continued list Mou county in Taishan, the old polity of Mou, which has nothing to do with Dongmou in Donglai.

sentences.zh: 羊祜傳詔以泰山之南武陽、牟、南城、梁父、平陽爲南城郡，是晉時已名牟縣也。

translations.literal: Yang Hu biography edict used Taishan’s Nanwuyang, Mou, Nancheng, Liangfu, Pingyang as Nancheng commandery; thus Jin times already named Mou county.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu’s biography records an edict that grouped Nanwuyang, Mou, Nancheng, Liangfu, and Pingyang in Taishan into Nancheng commandery, so by Jin times the place was already plain “Mou county.”

sentences.zh: 按：宋志一、《左傳》桓公十五年注「泰山牟縣」，均亦無「東」字，今據刪。

translations.literal: Comment: Song zhi 1, Zuo zhuan Duke Huan fifteenth year annotation “Taishan Mou county,” likewise lack “east” graph; now according delete.
translations.idiomatic: Song zhi 1 and Du Yu’s gloss on the fifteenth year of Duke Huan both speak of “Mou county in Taishan” without an extra “east,” so the stray character is removed.

sentences.zh: 長平馬校：縣已見前潁川郡，此誤複出。

translations.literal: Changping Ma’s collation: county already seen earlier Yingchuan commandery; this mistaken duplicate appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Changping: Ma’s Collation notes the county was already tallied under Yingchuan; this second listing is a mistaken repeat.

sentences.zh: 竺邑 《方校》：武陔傳，「沛國竹邑人」，此作「竺邑」，似誤。

translations.literal: Zhuyi Fang’s Collation: Wu Gai biography, “Pei Zhuyi person”; this writes “Zhuyi” (different graph); seems error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi: Fang’s Collation points out that Wu Gai’s biography calls him a native of Zhuyi in Pei with the “bamboo” radical, whereas here a near-homophone appears and is probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 斠注：魏志明紀、胡質傳引虞預晉書、宋書州郡志、水經睢水注引李奇說皆作「竹邑」。

translations.literal: Gloss: Wei zhi Ming annals, Hu Zhi biography cites Yu Yu Jin shu, Song shu provinces, Shui jing Sui River commentary cites Li Qi explanation all write “Zhuyi (bamboo).”
translations.idiomatic: Cross-checks in the Wei Chronicle’s basic annals, the biography of Hu Zhi citing Yu Yu’s Jin shu, the Song gazetteer, and Li Qi’s gloss in the Shui jing commentary on the Sui consistently spell the place with the bamboo graph.

sentences.zh: 竺邑即竹邑，本漢縣，有竹邑侯張壽碑。

translations.literal: Zhuyi is Zhuyi (bamboo), originally Han county, has Zhuyi marquis Zhang Shou stele.
translations.idiomatic: The intended name is Zhuyi, a Han county; a memorial stele for Marquis Zhang Shou of Zhuyi still attests it.

sentences.zh: 按：《漢志·上》、《續漢志·二》、《後漢書·明八王傳》、《吳志·薛綜傳》、《隋志·下》彭城郡符離下注並作「竹」。

translations.literal: Comment: Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 2, Hou Han shu eight Ming princes, Wu zhi Xue Zong, Sui zhi lower Pengcheng commandery Fuli below annotation all write “bamboo.”
translations.idiomatic: The upper Han treatise, fascicle two of the Continued Han, the lives of the Later Han’s eight Ming princes, Xue Zong’s biography in the Wu zhi, and the gloss on Fuli under Pengcheng in the lower Sui gazetteer all keep the bamboo radical.

sentences.zh: 蕃各本作「番」，今從宋本作「蕃」，與漢志下、《續漢志·二》合。

translations.literal: Fan various editions write “fan” (other graph); now follow Song edition as “Fan,” agree Hanshi lower, Xu Han zhi 2.
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses print a homophone of the place name, but the Song edition’s full form matches the lower Han treatise and fascicle two of the Continued Han.

sentences.zh: 縣八十三「三」，各本作「二」，今從殿本作「三」，與實領縣數合。

translations.literal: Counties eighty-three “three,” various editions read “two”; now follow palace edition as “three,” agrees actual county count.
translations.idiomatic: The tally “eighty-three counties” appears as “eighty-two” in most copies; the palace manuscript’s “three” matches the real number of counties governed.

sentences.zh: 易城漢志上、《續漢志·二》、後魏志上及後漢書劉虞傳並無「城」字。

translations.literal: Yicheng Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 2, Hou Wei zhi upper and Hou Han shu Liu Yu biography all lack “city” graph.
translations.idiomatic: For Yicheng, the upper Han treatise, fascicle two of the Continued Han, the upper Wei geography, and Liu Yu’s Later Han biography omit the extra graph “walled town.”

sentences.zh: 戶一萬八千一百「八千」，各本作「六千」，今從殿本作「八千」，與統計戶數相符。

translations.literal: Households one wan eight thousand one hundred “eight thousand,” various editions read “six thousand”; now follow palace edition as “eight thousand,” agrees statistical household count.
translations.idiomatic: The census line “eighteen thousand one hundred households” is corrupted to “sixteen thousand” in many witnesses; the palace manuscript’s “eight” tallies with the aggregate figures.

sentences.zh: 陰氣雍閼也「陰」下原有「陽」字。

translations.literal: Yin vapor congest block also below “yin” originally had “yang” graph.
translations.idiomatic: In the sentence about yin vapor dammed and stalled, an intrusive “yang” once stood after “yin.”

sentences.zh: 斠注：類聚六、御覽一六四引太康地記均無「陽」字。

translations.literal: Gloss: Yiwen leiju 6, Imperial Readings 164 cite Taikang geography record all lack “yang” graph.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel citations in Yiwen leiju, book 6, and Taiping yulan, scroll 164, quoting the Taikang geography, never show the extra “yang.”

translations.literal: Comment: lacking “yang” graph correct; now according delete.
translations.idiomatic: The shorter reading is sound, and the spurious graph is excised.

sentences.zh: 始平郡泰始二年置「二」，各本作「三」，今從宋本作「二」，與宋志三合。

translations.literal: Shiping commandery Taishi second year establish “two,” various editions read “three”; now follow Song edition as “two,” agrees Song zhi 3.
translations.idiomatic: The founding of Shiping commandery in the second year of Taishi is misdated as the third year in most texts; Song zhi 3 supports the second year, as does the Song exemplar.

sentences.zh: 徙都 疑此二字因涉下文「徙都長安」而誤衍。

translations.literal: Move capitalsuspect these two graphs because involved below text “move capital Chang’an” mistaken redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase “moved the capital” is probably a dittography prompted by “moved the capital to Chang’an” a few lines later.

sentences.zh: 李閏姚萇載記、魏書安定王燮傳皆作「李潤」。

translations.literal: Li Run (the Jin treatise corrupts the name with the graph for “intercalary month”): Yao Chang annals, Wei shu Prince of Anding Yuan Xie biography both write Li Run with the standard “moisten” graph.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Jin treatise writes Li with the “intercalary” graph, parallel sources such as Yao Chang’s annals and the Wei shu biography of Prince Anding Xie spell the place Li Run with the standard “moisten” character.

sentences.zh: 避文帝諱改也「文」，原誤作「景」，今改正。

translations.literal: Avoid Wendi taboo changed also “wen,” original mistakenly wrote “Jing”; now correct.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss should name Emperor Wen’s taboo, not “Jing”; the mistaken graph is corrected.

translations.literal: Ming’an “ming” original text read “yi.”
translations.idiomatic: For Ming’an the first character was wrongly copied as “suitable” instead of “dark.”

sentences.zh: 《畢校》：應作「冥安」，《元和郡縣志》以縣界冥水爲名。

translations.literal: Bi’s Collation: ought read “Ming’an”; Yuanhe commandery-county gazetteer uses county border Ming river as name.
translations.idiomatic: Bi’s Collation argues for “Ming’an,” the form preserved in the Yuanhe junxian zhi, which explains the name from the Ming River along the border.

translations.literal: Comment: Bi’s view correct; now according change.
translations.idiomatic: Bi’s judgment stands, and the text is emended.

translations.literal: Below same.
translations.idiomatic: The same correction applies to the entries that follow.

sentences.zh: 深泉考異：「淵泉」作「深泉」，避唐諱。

translations.literal: Shenquan variant: “Yuanquan” written “Shenquan,” avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenquan replaces Yuanquan to skirt the Tang taboo on “abyss.”

sentences.zh: 張駿分武威武興西平張掖酒泉建康西海西郡湟河晉興廣武合十一郡爲涼州 原缺「西海」，「廣武」誤作「須武」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》補改。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun divided Wuwei Wuxing Xiping Zhangye Jiuquan Jiankang Xihai Xijun Huanghe Jinxing Guangwu total eleven commanderies as Liangzhou originally lacked “Xihai,” “Guangwu” mistaken wrote “Xuwu”; now according Hou Wei shu Zhang Jun biography supplement emend.
translations.idiomatic: Where Zhang Jun grouped Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwueleven commanderies in allinto Liangzhou, the manuscript dropped Xihai and garbled “Guangwu” as “Xuwu”; both errors are repaired from the Later Wei history’s biography of Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 敦煌晉昌高昌西域都護戊己校尉玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州 原缺「高昌」，「戊己」誤作「張茂以」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》增改。

translations.literal: Dunhuang Jinchang Gaochang Western Regions protector Wuji colonel Yumen grand guard three commanderies three camps as Shazhou originally lacked “Gaochang,” “wuji” mistaken wrote “Zhang Mao yi”; now according Hou Wei shu Zhang Jun biography add change.
translations.idiomatic: The roster that makes Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, the Western Regions protector, the Wuji colonel, and the Yumen grand guardthree commanderies alongside three garrisonsinto Sha province originally omitted Gaochang and mangled “Wuji” into a phrase about Zhang Mao; the Later Wei biography of Zhang Jun supplies the fixes.

translations.literal: Jin again became Tianshui “Jin” ought read “Wei.”
translations.idiomatic: The word “Jin” should read “Wei”: Wei times again saw a Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏時有天水郡，見三國志姜維傳及注、楊阜傳、曹真傳、張既傳、閻溫傳。

translations.literal: Wei times had Tianshui commandery, see Sanguo zhi Jiang Wei biography and annotations, Yang Fu biography, Cao Zhen biography, Zhang Ji biography, Yan Wen biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wei already maintained a Tianshui commandery, documented in the lives of Jiang Wei (and Pei’s notes), Yang Fu, Cao Zhen, Zhang Ji, and Yan Wen.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平六年趙一清水經注釋三三：全祖望謂初平只四年，無六年，當作元年。

translations.literal: And Xiandi Chuping sixth year Zhao Yi Qing Shui jing zhu commentary 33: Quan Zuwang says Chuping only four years, no sixth year, ought read first year.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Xian’s sixth year of Chuping, Zhao Yi’s commentary to the Shui jing zhu cites Quan Zuwang’s remark that Chuping lasted but four years and should begin with the first year of that era, not a nonexistent sixth.

sentences.zh: 縣四十四各本作「縣三十三」，今從殿本作「縣四十四」，與統計實數合。

translations.literal: Counties forty-four various editions read “counties thirty-three”; now follow palace edition as “counties forty-four,” agrees statistical actual number.
translations.idiomatic: Where copies say “thirty-three counties,” the palace manuscript’s “forty-four” matches the actual tally in the tables.

sentences.zh: 蜀置 《畢校》：譙周《巴記》，建安六年劉璋分巴郡墊江以上爲巴西郡。

translations.literal: Shu establish Bi’s Collation: Qiao Zhou Ba record, Jian’an sixth year Liu Zhang divided Ba commandery Dianjiang above as Baxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Annotation on Shu’s foundation: Bi’s Collation cites Qiao Zhou’s Ba Record that in the sixth year of Jian’an Liu Zhang split off the region above Dianjiang in Ba commandery as Baxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 據此，則巴西郡劉璋時分置。

translations.literal: According this, then Baxi commandery Liu Zhang times divided establish.
translations.idiomatic: If that entry is sound, Baxi commandery was already peeled off while Liu Zhang still held Ba.

sentences.zh: 魚復各本作「魚腹」，今從宋本作「魚復」。

translations.literal: Yufu various editions write “fish belly”; now follow Song edition as “fish restore.”
translations.idiomatic: Most witnesses corrupt the name to the homophone meaning “fish belly,” yet the Song block preserves the ancient “fish-return” spelling.

sentences.zh: 漢志上、《續漢志·五》、華陽國志一、後漢書張堪傳、蜀志先主傳並作「魚復」。

translations.literal: Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 5, Huayang guo zhi 1, Hou Han shu Zhang Kan biography, Shu zhi First Lord biography all write “Yufu.”
translations.idiomatic: The upper Han treatise, fascicle five of the Continued Han, book one of the Huayang guo zhi, Zhang Kan’s Later Han biography, and the Shu zhi life of the First Lord all agree on Yufu.

sentences.zh: 初平元年劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡考異：劉焉以興平元年卒，子璋始爲益州牧，則初平元年璋尚未牧益州，「初平」當爲「興平」之訛。

translations.literal: First year Chuping Liu Zhang divided Ba commandery establish Yongning commandery variant: Liu Yan died first year Xingping, son Zhang began be Yizhou shepherd, then first year Chuping Zhang not yet shepherd Yizhou, “Chuping” ought be “Xingping’s” scribal error.
translations.idiomatic: The line dating Yongning commandery to the first year of Chuping, when Liu Zhang supposedly split Ba, is dubious: Liu Yan died at the outset of Xingping, and only his son Zhang then took stewardship of Yizhou; in the first year of Chuping Zhang had no mandate there, so “Chuping” is plainly a corruption of Xingping.

translations.literal: Tanzhi original text read “Zitan.”
translations.idiomatic: The two graphs of Tanzhi were reversed to the meaningless sequence “Zitan.”

sentences.zh: 斠注：兩漢志、華陽國志四並作「談指」。

translations.literal: Gloss: Two Han gazetteers, Huayang guo zhi 4 both write “Tanzhi.”
translations.idiomatic: Both Han dynastic gazetteers and book four of the Huayang guo zhi spell the county Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 按：漢書昭帝紀、前漢紀十六亦作「談指」。

translations.literal: Comment: Han shu Emperor Zhao annals, Qian Han ji 16 also write “Tanzhi.”
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao annals in the Han shu and scroll sixteen of the Qian Han ji record the same form.

translations.literal: Now according transpose correct.
translations.idiomatic: The characters are transposed back into order.

translations.literal: Wulian original text read “Wujian.”
translations.idiomatic: The county appears as “Wujian,” importing the graph for “sword” by mistake.

sentences.zh: 斠注：兩漢志、宋志、華陽國志四、水經溫水注皆作「毋歛」。

translations.literal: Gloss: Two Han gazetteers, Song gazetteer, Huayang guo zhi 4, Shui jing Wen River commentary all write “Wulian.”
translations.idiomatic: The two Han treatises, the Song gazetteer, the Huayang guo zhi, and the Wen River passage of the Shui jing unanimously read Wulian.

translations.literal: Comment: “sword” is mistaken graph; now change.
translations.idiomatic: The intrusive graph is wrong and is replaced.

sentences.zh: 毋掇漢志上「掇」作「棳」，師古曰其字從木。

translations.literal: Wuzhuo Hanshi shang “zhuo” writes “zhuo” (tree radical), Shigu says its graph follows wood.
translations.idiomatic: For Wuzhuo the upper Han treatise writes the second syllable with the tree radical, and Yan Shigu remarks that the character belongs to the wood classifier.

translations.literal: Shui jing Wen River commentary also writes “Wuzhuo” (tree radical).
translations.idiomatic: The Wen River commentary in the Shui jing preserves the same wooden-graph spelling.

translations.literal: Tanfeng “tan,” various editions write “duo” (bell).
translations.idiomatic: At Tanfeng the name should carry the “sword-hilt” graph, but copies substitute the homophone for “hand-bell.”

sentences.zh: 宋本及音義作「鐔」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Song edition and phonological glosses write “tan”; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: The Song printing and the pronunciation glosses keep the correct graph, and we follow them.

sentences.zh: 與漢志上、《續漢志·五》、宋志四、華陽國志四、水經溫水注合。

translations.literal: Agrees Hanshi shang, Xu Han zhi 5, Song zhi 4, Huayang guo zhi 4, Shui jing Wen River commentary.
translations.idiomatic: That reading matches the upper Han treatise, fascicle five of the Continued Han, fascicle four of the Song gazetteer, book four of the Huayang guo zhi, and the Wen River commentary.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年至夜郎二郡 王遜傳：「元帝加遜安南將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: Yongjia second year reach Yelang two commanderies Wang Xun biography: “Yuandi added Xun Defender-in-Chief of the South, inspector as before.”
translations.idiomatic: On the Yongjia-era expansion down to the two Yelang commanderies, Wang Xun’s biography quotes the emperor’s rescript: “The court invested Xun as Defender-in-Chief of the South while leaving him inspector, as before.”

sentences.zh: 遜表請改分牂牁爲平夷郡，分建寧爲夜郎郡，改益州爲晉寧郡，事皆施行。

translations.literal: Xun memorial requested change divide Zangge as Pingyi commandery, divide Jianning as Yelang commandery, change Yizhou as Jinning commandery, affairs all implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to carve Zangge into Pingyi commandery, spin Jianning off as Yelang commandery, and rename Yizhou as Jinning commandery, and every item of the plan was carried out.

translations.literal: End of quotation: it conflicts with this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that narrative disagrees with the arrangement recorded in this chapter.
